EARLY REVIEW: NOT REPRESENTATIVE OF FINAL
DISCLAIMER: I've played the Wii U version, so despite not finishing it on PC my full thoughts still stand and are accurate.
Steam doesn't have an option to just say "mixed", or whatever. I don't hate Lost World, but I really don't like it either. Ultimately, I'm leaving this as a not-recommended, but I'd say pick it up should it ever go on sale for at least $15. There's a good game in there somewhere, it's just not there.
So Lost World. Basically, Lost World. To put it into perspective, if you didn't like the Wii U original, well this may not change too much.
A decent Sonic game that becomes a hard recommend due to poor execution, cheap level design, and it's strange desire to constantly change the rules of how the game plays....for the worse.
Pick it up on sale.
And for the record....I honestly don't really like this game. It's a hard sell at this moment: A Sonic game where it's level design comes from being either cheap or way too gimmicky for it's own good. It's hard to adapt to the game's large list of controls and game mechanics because it really likes to shake things up often, usually leaving in some mixed results.
First, the good: Presentation is pretty good. The art style is nice, and the music (Despite not being really "Sonic") is definitely a great if forgettable romp. I guess what I can really say is that Lost World is really "Lost Potential". There's so many interesting concepts, so many interesting ideas, that just get lost in the game. More on that later.
It's mostly polished, it's mostly alright, it's mostly decent. The issue that breaks the game is really just the questionable execution and the really annoying things about it that make Lost World one of the more frustrating experiences I've had in awhile. It's honestly hard to talk about what I really like about the game a lot, because I don't necessarily hate it. I think it's actually good, it's just so flawed that it's hard to think of what the game really does right at this point.
The port is nice though, although the resolution is a bit funky for me. The game runs a lot more consistent at 60fps although the cutscenes run at 30fps. Video options are pretty barebones but the optimization is great, so it's not too big of a deal. This can run on a lot of low-end computers too. A lot of the new stuff like controller prompts and such look ugly as hell, so there's some pretty low areas in terms of polish. It's clear that this is more of a budget port, but it's not bad at all. Just not too fantastic.
UPDATE: The game may or may not be a bit a hassle to run for those with low-end computers. Some have stated the game runs perfect with even Intel HD Graphics while others struggle to even get 20 FPS. My PC Build is an absolute beast so this isn't a problem for me at all.
The story is also just unbearable to play through. Everybody in the game are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. Sonic acts so arrogant and cocky that it honestly makes him a bit unlikable, and Tails sounds way too pretentious for his own good. The game's jokes fall completely flat, and it's just not a confident story that delivers. What the hell, like I play Sonic games for their story.
And it sucks too, because this game has some seriously great concepts and ideas that could had very well turned Sonic out for the better. But it doesn't, because of clunky execution. Parkour is something that easily fixes the problems of you being stopped by running into a wall, but running into walls and in general wall-running just doesn't entirely feel right, and is in general really clumsy. The real problem is that Lost World constantly changes and shifts the rules of how Sonic controls, without much explanation or any real reason too. There's a level where you're a snowball, a level with stealth-segments, and a level where you glide around in the air. The constant shifts in level design and pacing make this game really hard to play, as if grasping on to it's sort of finicky controls weren't hard enough.
Bosses aren't even a challenge. Zazz can be taken down in both of his acts so easily it's almost sad.
The real flaw here is it's level-design. Lost World has an interesting idea: Make the levels flat, but compensate this with multiple routes. Unfortunately, I don't think Sonic has ever worked that easily in a flat environment, even if the game was designed for said flat-environment. As mentioned before, with the constant shifts in how you play, so a lot of the levels don't even follow the same mechanics as others. And it's just cheap, too. There are enemies in the game that can just kill you in one hit. Bam. Their placement in the levels don't exactly help either, making for some really frustrating moments in the game. For the multiple-paths idea, it's not half-bad, but it's weird that for a Sonic game, a lot of the alternate paths generally waste your time more, rather then saving it.
Questionable design decisions hold it back too. Why aren't there checkpoints in the time attack? Especially when the game is so cheap that one death leads you back to the start? Why are these bonus items even on there, and what's the point? They're almost completely useless and only the wisp ones are helpful for completing Omochao's challenges, which is a boring checklist of boring things to do but can only do 3 specific randomized missions at a time. Color Powers are just poorly tacked-on for no reason.
If you aren't reading the English I'm saying, basically what you have on your hands is a game that just has no idea what it wants to be. A platformer? A pinball game? Stealth? Some of the levels are alright, while others are just an absolute pain to play through, to the point of just burning me out on the game completely.
So overall, what do I think of the game? It's better to pick it up on sale. Flawed execution, garbage level design, laughable story, it all holds it back, but there's still a good game in there somewhere. If you love Sonic, or express interest in trying this game out, then give it a shot. $30 is really stretching it for a really flawed game that's been out for 2 years now though.

Endless runners aren't really my thing, and Last Knight didn't do enough to convince me otherwise. It does have a great sense of style going for it, and the graphics are pretty, if nothing mindblowing, but the gameplay quickly wears thin and I often feel like I'm not the one at fault when something bad happens.
And for those of you who game on a laptop, beware: this game takes a lot more power to run than you'd think. It ran fine when I first tried it back in Early Access, but starting it up recently it managed a few frames a second just trying to play the intro movie. Absurd, right? So my first instinct was to skip it. Oops, bad decision, turns out the game is bugged and that makes it crash. First thing I did was go to the forums and found out you could comment out the intro movie in the .ini, though for someone who isn't technically inclined this would be more of a serious problem. Tried the Rogue Rider mode and with all the graphics down I think there were maybe 4 triangles on the map selection screen, which wiggled wildly, and even then it still barely ran. Luckily the game itself managed somewhat better optimization than that, though it still didn't seem to run as well as it used to. Apparently you need a decent rig to run a prettied-up phone game.
All in all Last Knight didn't leave a very good impression on me. If you do, however, happen to love endless runners and have a modern gaming rig this seems like a pretty bog standard but nicely polished iteration on the idea with a quirky sense of style that might be up your alley. Aside from the technical issues I experienced there's not much objectively bad about this game, I just didn't really enjoy it all that much.

Alright. Let me start off by saying that this was my first "Ultimate Ninja Storm" game that I've completed. So if you've never played one of these, I can help you out. First off, this is a 3D fighting game that is based off of the anime "Naruto". This game in particular takes place during the "Fourth Great Ninja War". If you have never seen the show or have never read the manga of Naruto, it's going to be a bit confusing for you. I would recommend watching the show or at least doing a bit of research on Naruto if you want to understand this story. Anyways, you can move Naruto around the game map and talk to other characters  to progress the story. Although, this is honestly kind of a little pointless. There's barely anything on the map aside from a few collectibles every now and then, and you can buy pretty much every thing you find in the in game shops. And sometimes, it takes quite awhile to get from one area to another. While I thought the world was pretty cool at first, it got pretty tedious running back and forth.  If you were expecting a big open world game to explore in the Naruto universe, prepare to be disappointed. Anyways, the story is mostly made up of cutscenes which can be preeeeety lengthy at times. There's this one chapter where there's a cutscene that's like 50 minutes long. So if you plan to see the story, you'd better be prepared to sit back and watch. The story also has boss battles ranging from fighting regular characters to fighting massive monsters. The fights are great and in the middle of some of them, a mini cutscene activates where your character moves on their own and you have to do quick-time events for them to do a pretty cool, flashy move. These are only in the story though, not in the normal game. So if you enjoy looking at em, you'll have to replay that story mission. If you don't like QTE's, well then you don't have to worry too much as they're not in every battle and you don't need to do them much anyways. And the graphics of this game look very nice. The PC version compliments the art style nicely and everything looks so soft and smooth. It is a console port though so don't expect super high textures and jaw dropping visuals or anything. It's locked to 30 fps btw. That's kind of disappointing but the way the game plays with its smooth animations kind of makes up for it. It's still playable if you ask me. Also, something really weird which hasn't gotten fixed from past UNS games is the lip syncing of characters. Their mouths don't match with what the characters say at all and they still move even after the voice of the character has stopped which is just embarrasing. Just letting you know if you notice this happening, there's nothing wrong with your game. Moving on to the gameplay, the characters all have their standard combo attacks and can use special attacks which consume "chakra". This chakra can also be used to do a super move which uses up all your chakra and looks pretty cool! When you're fighting in the story against AI, their difficulty raises depending on the story conditions. For the most part, they are pretty easy. But those bosses that I mentioned earlier can also be pretty cheap at times. For example, some parts of the story make you fight multiple enemies at once and they are so annoying trying to hit you all at the same time. For them, sometimes you can't just fight normally and try to do combos. And you might end up having to just spam some moves to get them heck away from you while you focus on one of em. But like I said, most of the fights are pretty fair and there aren't too many bosses like that until you get towards the end of the game. Another thing to mention is that there's a ton of characters in this Naruto game. All the regulars like Naruto, Sasuke, Sakura, Tsunade, Kakashi, etc. And a lot of characters from Shippuden like Raikage, Mizukage, Kazekage Gaara, etc. Also, this version is Full Burst which contains all of the DLC from the regular version and the most notable addition being the extra DLC chapter which focuses on a fight with the two Uchiha brothers vs a powerful villian who I won't spoil. However, I suggest you only do this fight if you're really brave or want to complete everything the game has to offer. As this fight is far more difficult than anything in the regular game and he is by far the cheapest piece of garbage in the entire game. (I eventually beat it, but I cannot tell you how many times I died) Overall, I say it's a decent fighting game. It's worth a try but it is far from perfect.
PROS
-Excellent graphics
-Follows Naruto story
-Tons of characters
-Decent fighting system
-Great animations
CONS
-Bad character lip sync
-Barren game world
-Locked to 30 fps
-Some cheap boss battles
-Long cutscenes
If you're a Naruto fan, I recommend checking this one out. If you're not and just want a fighting game, feel free to get this on sale. But there's definitely better fighters out there.

Last Knight, developed by Toco Games, is a PC game in which you will take on the role of squire, or knight in training. You will be faced with many different challenges, as well as many different modes to play in. This is a 3D rogue runner game. What I mean by this is that the levels are always going to be randomly generated, and you, on your horse, will constantly be going. You will have to joust enemies as they block your path. You will need to collect coins, and in some modes food.
Graphically you are looking at a game that looks very well polished. There's definitely some roughness to the polygons used, but that just fits the game. There's also an impressive amount of different play modes, when it comes to the story portion of the game. You will get to see the game from 3/4 view, 1st person, and top down. Making sure that all of these different views felt polished is quite impressive. There's also the fact that the levels are randomly generated, and the differing areas, path, cave, forest, etc flow seamlessly.
The music of the game is a very uplifting, medieval themed soundtrack that will have to getting into the game as you dodge the obstacles, take out the enemies, and collect the rewards.
The controls of the game are your WASD combo, well most of them. You are going to be using W to bring your lance down, and A and D to move from side to side. You will also use the space bar to jump, but in this game timing is everything, so you are going to have to be mindful of when you jump.
Alright so there's a lot to this game. There's really three complete modes in this game. You have an endless runner mode where you will basically try to last as long as possible in one shot. You will gain quests to complete, and you will of course be trying to collect as much treasure as possible. I will tell you this, though it is not clear, to complete the quests you receive you have to have the correct rider unlocked. That's one of the reasons you are collecting treasure, there's also power ups that can help you, but you will first have to gain enough coins/treasure to unlock those as well. There are several different modes within this mode, and they increase in difficulty and also have pre-requisites before they can become unlocked.
The second overall mode is the story mode. To truly master this mode you will have to play all the levels in the 3/4 view, 1st person, and top down. Each mode has the same overall story, but you will have to beat the levels in each mode. Unfortunately you can't pick the mode that's most comfortable for you, once you've unlocked it and continue the story from where you left off. There's going to be tons of knights, spiders, frogs, dragons, skeletons, and more that will stand in your way of saving the kingdom, but if you can make it through it all, a special prize awaits you.
The third overall mode is probably my favorite, as well as being the most frustrating mode. In this mode you will see the truly rogue-ness of the game. An entire world will be randomly generated for you, and you will have to navigate through said world, but if you die, the entire world goes boom. So there's no redos, there's no chance of continuing on after you have defeated 7 regions, you will have to start from scratch, even in the armor and items department. So as you can see it's amazing to have this randomly generated world where nothing is the same during any playthrough, but if you die the entire thing goes out the door, which to me causes me much stress. I would love to have the ability to be able to come back from a death, perhaps with a penalty, and continue on in the world. It just seems like such a waste of design to throw away something like that so quickly. There is one other thing that is a bit frustrating about this mode, and it doesn't really have to do with the gameplay, its the freaking overworld map, I can't seem to smoothly look over it, its always crooked and I feel that there's some magical stopping point for the camera which makes looking at different sides of the castle damn near impossible, or just selecting the next realm you want to be in.

Ever wondered "what if?"
If you have ever wanted to be a trade mogul making billions....
A miner amassing riches extracting the most precious metals of the galaxy and selling them for profit...
A soldier fighting wars on all fronts in massive fleets...
A researcher studying the vast mysteries of space...
A manufacturer and dealer of an insurmountable level of munitions and arms...
A PROFITEER - Then EVE is for you.
You can be anyone in EVE. You can do anything, at any time, for any reason. EVE is an open universe waiting for you to jump in and make a name for yourself. The sheer level of activities on offer is mind boggling. Sure, the FREE TO PLAY isn't really free. Alpha characters, as they are known, are very limited to what they can do. That being said, they can still do almost everything there is to do in EVE, not to mention MAKE A KILLING. If you want more, sure. You can pay. Or, you can buy PLEX with IN GAME money (ISK) and never have to pay your subscription again, since PLEX (Pilot License Extention) can be redeemed for 30 days of game time.
I love running military missions, killing pirates, mining and running HUGE pirate hunting ops called Incursions. 10-12 hours of incursion running pays for an entire month of game time for me (about 3-4 hours a day, 2-3 days a month). I fly a Rattlesnake battleship equipped with cruise missiles that have the capability of locking a target over 90km away, and travelling a maxium distance of just under 130km. With my microwarpdrive and target painter in hand, a volley of these missiles from several launchers at a time usually means certain death for nearly any but the largest of battleships. And even then, they are not nearly close enough to do anything to me...before it is too late.
The satisfaction of making things go boom in this game is indescribable. If you want to forge your own path in the stars, EVE is for you.

You could have even used the coins collected in game to purchase extra lives, giving them more functionality than just adding to your score.
So I am a little disappointed in some of the game mechanic choices but over all I'd still recommend giving Last Knight a go just for it's brilliant concept but maybe wait until it's on sale.

Last Knight is a runner game frequently compared to Temple Run but  honestly feels alot more like a game based around the Warthog level in Crash Bandicoot 1. There is a mode that allows endless running but there is also a story mode and an addictive rougelike mode. Hats, power ups and a food system offer a surprising amount of content for what appears to be just another runner.  It is a good looking  game running in the Unreal engine and has tons of charm. Accidentally making your rider eat a giant meat stacked burger and then fearing the sight of floating chicken wings is definitely a unique and rather comedic experience.
The sound effects and music are very well done and perfectly fit the theme of the game. Most importantly controls are tight and responsive making moments when a rival rider or monster knock you off your horse feel fair. The rag doll effects when you best your foes is a very enjoyable effect that never gets old. Though this is not the kind of games you would play for hours on end, it's more of a go to game when you have a bit of spare time and want a simple yet challenging gaming session.
This is one of the very few Early Access games that I am glad I supported, friendly dev that is open to suggestions and a released product that feels complete and polished. If you are one of those people that stare at your Steam list wondering what you should play I can think of no better go to game than Last Knight Rouge Rider Edition.

Telltale's Tales from the Borderlands is a good example of Telltale's ability to tell an in-depth story that is immersive and fun.
Pros
- Very good story.
- Very good audio: Both in music and voice acting.
- This is one of Telltale's longer stories.
- A pleasant mix of Telltale's "action" mechanic and story exploration.
- There is a "comedic" or light hearted side to the game.
- You get to play as two characters.
Cons
- At points this game's "action" feels more like an interactive story as opposed to MW4 or Halo 5 action.
- The story is typical of several Telltale titles in the fact that no matter what choices you choose to make, you reach the exact same ending either way.
- The game's comedy may not be appealing to everyone. It's not bad, but some won't find it nearly as funny as others.
Final Thoughts: While the lack of permanent choices that change the ending can be disappointing, the story is very good. If you're looking for a more interactive story as opposed to an action game, this game is well worth your time.

Dead Island does a great job mixing a first person shooter/ melee game with role playing elements including weapons capable of being upgraded and modified to improve critical hit chance and add elemental or bleeding/ poison effects, four "character classes" with unique abilities and skill trees, and quest after quest after quest! About the only thing missing is armor ( would love to find leather jackets/ riot gear/shields).  My brother and I have logged tons of hours in Left4Dead 1 and 2, and this game feels like the logical "next step" in our Co-op progression.
The inclusion of vehicles to travel quickly across maps (and rack up some hit and run XP) adds a new level of fun that I didn't expect, along with the occasional frustration as the vehicles become hoplessly stuck in the environment. Full Disclosure: This almost only ever happens when I drive, and I drive at top speed most of the time. Even getting stuck (if it is not in a mission critical vehicle) can be fun and add a new level of excitement if it occurs in an area heavily populated by undead.
Many of the elements I have mentioned are not "polished", and while other games do them better, I can't think of a game that puts them all together in such a cohesive manner ( I haven't played Dying Light yet).
I owned the original game, and picked up the Definitive Edition during the Halloween sale so my brother and I could play together, and aside from Witcher 3, this game easily has the best "game-to-dollars spent" ratio I have seen.
Playing Single Player is creepier, but the game seems to scale the difficulty down, and during coop looted money is shared and most loot items are availble to all characters.
While many reviewers are recommending Dying Light over this title, I think that It stands on its own, and is a "must play" if you haven't already done so.

I came back to this game after a while, mainly for nostalgic reasons. My experience is rather mixed.
The environment is wonderful, the story interesting and the in-game universe has a great potential. There's many races to choose from and the way the world works is amazing. Unfortunately, this potential is unfulfilled because so far there's very little difference between the stories of various races and the game itself makes the player focus on other things (mostly PvP). The RPG element is kinda taken away because your dialogue choices don't really matter.
However, every steampunk fan should try this game. It's a great inspiration for costumes and/or steampunk props, some armor sets are kinda cool and there's not only steam guns but steam swords too! (not sure how that works but whatever) Plus the soundtrack is A+ and gives the game a nice touch.
Possibly the worst thing (or two things) is that it's pay-to-win and if something goes wrong the support won't help you because they're gone. No updates for months, no bug fixes, dead forums. Many players experience problems with loading or other things and there's no response from the devs or anyone. Some people are complaining about the auto-combat feature but it's completely optional. Turn it off.
My recommendation would go like this:
Try it. Play the game for a while and see how you like it.
But don't take it too seriously and don't use your real money on it.
TL;DR
+ environment and lore
+ soundtrack
+ skills animations
+ detailed weapons/armor
+ wheelie on a steambike
+/- auto-combat feature (optional)
+/- focused on PvP at higher levels
- non-existent support
- pay-to-win
- bugs, bugs, bugs

Pros:
+Tight, punchy shooting makes the combat immensely satisfying. This is helped by great blood effects (unlike other shooters, streams of blood gush from enemy injuries with every bullet)
+The levels are intelligently designed to allow strategy and stealth. There's no shortage of terrain, foliage, trees, and accesible houses to let you both hide from enemies or intelligently take the fight to them.
+The stealth system itself is solid, if a little finnicky at times.
+The environments, weapons, and particle effects can look gorgeous when all the settings are cranked up.
+No shortage of exciting, player-manufactured (non-scripted) moments. Since you spend most of the game alone (no AI partners like in other shooters), the game has a legitmately thrilling one-man-army element. There's something adrenaline-pumping about infiltrating a large village full of Nazis, silently taking out some of them, being spotted, and engaging in a frantic firefight through the village streets, buildings, and surrounding forest areas.
+The large environments help make the game feel less linear.
Cons:
+HIDEOUS character models made worse by robotic, expressionless animations.
+Optimization could be better.
+Gameplay, despite being fun and sastisying, is pretty repetetive as far as objectives are concerned. Most of it involves taking out enemy vehicles, eliminating all enemies in a certain area, blowing up enemy territory, or collecting an important item within hostile areas.
+The story is impossible to care about thanks to mediocre presentation, equally lackluster writing, and bland voice acting.
+A few, infrequent glitches here and there (mostly some objet pop-in and enemis clipping through objects)
+The enemy AI is scattered all over the place. Sometimes the enemies will put up a legitimately good fight by flanking you, throwing grenades, and overwhelming you by sheer force (especially rushing your location). Other times they'll act brain-dead, staying in cover and popping out their heads to allow you a headshot or blindly firing in your direction with no strategy.
+The stealth kill animations are bit too long, sometimes giving enemies a chance to spot you in the act.
Overall: I can honestly say this game's worth buying and playing all the way through... if on sale. The gameplay's a ton of fun, but the overall package feels unpolished in some areas. This isn't helped by the fact that the story flat-out sucks, which might make it hard for some to get invested in the gameplay itself. But despite that, the vulnerable but resilient one-man-army element of the gameplay makes it more than worth checking out. Recommended

Last Knight: Rogue Rider Edition, is one of the those amazing games that steam fails to promote fairly.
( notes , I got this game on April while it was on early access and i have a few hours on game-play but offline so it was not recorded, and I stopped updating it but since I saw it fully released now I updated and started playing again )
This game is really something , I liked it ever since I played it the first time although there were some glitches and Serious Framedrops at the beginning which stopped me from playing this game at first , but they are all fixed now and i'm enjoying this game a lot which is why I am making this review
To hit the point early, Whats not to like ? This game has beautiful artwork style, outstanding graphics, interactive story, great gameplay, Unlockables , Customizations, Secrets, Achievements , Trading cards, Stats , Controller supports and it also works beautifully on a keyboard and mouse so its got everything.
It is basically a running game, With Medieval touch, You're a knight on a horse the character keeps running, you dodge stuff jump And use your spear to thrust and the game gets better and better the more you play.
It supports huge screens with the resolution options, and while there it also has full graphics settings and the game is not that demanding with requirements I have a very normal laptop with a small Nvidia gpu and running this perfectly.
The game has some modes and stuff that makes it more entertaining, Such as Powerups to improve your strength by purchasing various items, unlocking quests for different characters throughout Endless mode ( which is really fun and hard ), More unlockables as you play through the game.
The game has (Mutators) which are more unlockables you unlock by getting (chivalry) points , they alter how the game is , For an example, one of them can turn this game into a first person view, and many more that changes the world and everything ( wont spoil it any further ) but they are brilliant
There also a "New world" Mode that is a randomly generated world you choose your path as you go on it has powerups and secrets and hats ! ( for customizing character )
And it is considered a Rogue-like , it spends a few seconds generating the new world ( a map for you to travel on ) and if you die its game over in this mode and you have to generate a new one, it is very different from the base game, you have a health Bar and find food to regain Hp, and after ever level you open up an inventory to upgrade your state and abilities.
And 4 other Fun modes to waste hours and hours on : )
Just by looking at those store Screenshots you can tell that this game is fun, Thats exactly the type of graphics I like in a video game, The water reflection, the trees the lights are so addictive and fun and the Animations with it are truly outstanding.
The game's soundtracks are really great, it brings out the medieval sense to this game along with this artwork.
I especially like the challenges in this game, it gets harder by the minute, faster and requires precision and more crazy stuff popping out and dragons ! you can't have a game with knights in it without dragons I always say !
The character designs are brilliant I love how they add this "Comedy" Touch to the game while maintaining its realistic forum and story.
So Overall.
- Pros :
1 - Wonderful Graphics, Animations, Artwork, Character designs, Style, Soundtrack
2 - Great addictive entertaining game-play, and a long story.
3 - The game takes a while to finish and with the challenges and modes it could be at least 20 hours to begin with and i'm looking at more hours : )
4 - Unlockables, Mutators that alters the game, Unlocking new characters , Customizing your own character and horse, Purchasing PowerUps, Endless mode for laughs and giggles ( and more secrets ) brings out more hours
5 - VERY fair store price ! I mean for this game you'd expect it to AT LEAST hit 14,99$  but this ? This is a great deal!
- Cons
1 - I feel the game is still not 100% optimized it COULD be that my laptop is just old , because when I minisize the game and bring it back up it freezes for a few seconds and takes time to start sometimes, Not sure if this should be a con because its the game or not a con because my laptop is getting old
This game is a must have for all you out there that enjoys those Runner games where you keep dodging stuff because this should be one of the tops, Everything about this game I just love so much I dare to say that you NEED to buy this game if you liked how it looks in the store

------[Introducting myself and reflecting on past naruto games] ------- Before I start this if you have not watched or read naruto up to its current point, You should catch up right now. Watch/Read the Pein arc before playing this game. I'm a naruto veteran, I've watched the 1st and second series, read all the manga, and most importantly played a lot of naruto games. The original naruto ultimate Ninja series was great and had a streetfighter/mortal kombat combo set and basic fighting mechnaics with interesting characters and alternate forms. They were amazing, This is my first naruto storm game and it was intimidating to me at first but after the prologue I felt very welcomed.
[Storm 3 Review]------ Storm 3 brings me in with an amazing boss fight against the nine tailed fox, Hooking me already, with an excellent opening battle. Throughout the game the combat (if you're new to it like I am) takes some time but it is not too hard to grasp and with time you get better and better, Specially being able to practice against AI before you go into story mode. Your scores in story mode depend how well you do in battle, it is better for you to use combos and fight and work up to your ultimate jutsu(S rating usually) rather than using ultimate jutsu continuesly to win a fight(D rating usually). The story is rich and definately changes some scenes up from the original material from the Manga. I enjoyed all of the story and it had me in tears many times because of how well it can make you feel emotional; if you know anything about naruto and his story you'll definately get to tears a couple of times in this games. The combat system like I said isnt too hard to grasp but in story mode it can be lackluster when you keep doing the same old same old on naruto himself, so its best in my opinion to play this game in small icrimants rather than in one playthrough. The multiplayer brings challanges and keeps everything fresh and you definately have a hard time against many online opponents, the game does not prepare you for what is online, so it for sure is fresh but will take practice(You'll have to know the combat inside and out from basic combos to mastering when you use your substitution/baiting out subs). Graphics are amazing, Ultimate Jutsus are amazing especially with the welcomed addition of the samurai characters(My favorite characters in the game). The ending of the story was a complete twist from the original material AND THAT REALLY MADE ME ENJOY IT A WHOLE LOT MORE. I thought I saw the ending I had read in the manga coming but it wasnt that specific ending and that surprise factor gets you in wanting more from this game and for sure makes you want to buy Storm 4  this game definately hyped me up for Naruto Storm 4. On a typical number scale, I give naruto storm 3 a 8/10.

A very fun game with solid gameplay that now has been remastered with better graphics and rebalanced gameplay.

The original game looked already pretty sweet, this DE version looks more crispy and they have improved some graphics effects such as godrays and bloom. I can't really call the improved textures 'HD' everywhere, but it does look a lot better then the original textures.  The only thing they have messed up is the water reflections unfortunately, the reflections now looks a bit blurry instead of sparkling.


Besides the graphics they have done a complete overhaul on the game iself. They have improved the driving in the game, it was a bit sluggish and now it feels smooth. They have improved a lot of quests by improving markers so it is more clear now where you have to place quest objects in the game.

They also rebalanced the loot value, the repair cost of weapons and in general the amount of money you gain in the game. In the original game you could upgrade your entire inventory and had plenty of money to repair your weapons. Now the money drains real quick due to very high repair costs. I personally don't really like how they have rebalanced it. You now have to be much more conservative with attacking zombies and sometimes even have to avoid them (run passed them like a sissy), because you don't have enough money to repair all your weapons constantly. So the old hack & slash gameplay now has been replaced (to some extend) with avoiding zombies. And avoiding zombies in this game does not deliver great gameplay due to a almost not working crouch/stealth mechanic. It is still a lot of fun the way it is, but I liked the original game balance more.

As for bugs/glitches and performance, it is all pretty smooth. The only bugs I encountered are AI sometimes clipping through objects (cars) and sometimes waypoint markers do not show on the map properly and you have to reset the waypoint. The performance itself is fine. I get a solid 80+ fps on maxed settings (plus 8x supersample), compared to 200fps with the original version of the game with the same settings. So obviously this new DE version does take up a lot more resources, but nothing to worry about.

And for the ones that have never played the original game, you will get a lot of game content for your bucks. All playable characters have more or less their own campaign. The campaigns will have the same side quests, but the story quests are all for the most part different with every character. A lot of people play this game as coop, but it is also very doable on your own as single player (SP is more fun IMO).
Small edit: I forgot to mention that they have also changed the skybox (clouds) in this new DE version. The old version had nice fluffy white clouds and now the game (beach map) has clouds like a heavy stormfront is coming in. Still great skybox and clouds, but I liked the original 'weather' more.
Verdict: 80/100

This game is fun. I'll just put that out there to start off. From a personal standpoint, I love the entire concept of it. A real gritty, tactical FPS. But before I go off on a tangeant like that, I'll sum up the pros and cons real quick:
• Excellent gunplay
Like, seriously. The weaponry is so satisfying. I got this game way back, back when there was just one weapon - the SMG. Even then, it was awesome. Now they have added two new weapons; an Assault Rifle, and a Pistol.. Thing. Either way, there's just something very satisfying about managing to headshot someone down a corridor, all sneaky beaky like.
• Environments
From the few maps there are, already it's clear a lot of time and effort is put into things. The attention to detail really shows, with some of the more lush/open maps (such as one that randomly changes setting every now and then) being extremely well done. The layout is also rather cool, as communicating with a squad and moving through a building feels very, very satisfying.
• The Suit/UI
From passive noises, to the dynamic of the HUD projected onto a proper model of the visor, the in-game UI feels very realistic, and looks badass. After being hit several times, the suit HUD even reacts, malfunctioning. This gives you a sound muffling effect as well, as if all electronics just shut down. And it pays off, resulting in a really immersive experience. The best part though? There's a key that lets you raise and lower the helmet visor - meaning if you wanna play without a HUD, you can.
• AI
Combat AI is rather reactive; it could do with being better, but as it stands, it is still rather formidable and entertaining to play against. Even alone, they can be challenging. Countless times I've gotten to the end of a section, with only two combat training droids to go, only to be flanked by them at the last second. Not fun, but a testament to how much you have to pay attention in this game to noise, as well as visuals.
• Not much content
At the time of writing this review (03/10/2016), the only real missions are; a handful of "Search and Destroy" style levels where you have to shoot and destroy all combat training droids in a map, A few missions where you have to trigger switches while avoiding combat droids, and two story missions - one being where you have to break into a secure compound and extract information, the other where you have to extract information from a science lab station. While both are cool, the game does get stale after a while, however multiplayer PvP is definitely fun (although I suck at that).
• Slow development time
From what I've heard, the game only has one full time developer due to financial issues. While that is rather.. Well, disappointing, it does testify as to how good this guy is. It's gonna take a lot of time for new content to be worked on (and at this rate, the game to be finished), but over the past couple of years there has been a few new additions - a couple of maps (rather large ones), and two new weapons. This definitely isn't a game to play if you want it right away, right now.
• Playerbase
There tends to not be as many players nowadays, most likely due to the slow development time. This game isn't going to be finished any time soon. This does mean that there is only one or two full matches on at a time, if you are lucky, and they tend to be PvP. If you want to play on Co-op, then let your friends know; you are highly unlikely to find anyone online.
• Server Hosting
While most servers tend to be really, really good, there are a few issues. The way server hosting works is, instead of having the ability to host your own server, you join an empty server and claim it as your own. This means you can change settings (such as password and player limit) and then you basically are happy as Larry. While that system works, it (used to be) very, very frustrating if you just wanted to play co-op with friends, and ended up with three other random people joining. And then your friends end up hosting their own, and the same goes on and on.
This game is good as it is, but it isn't exactly a full game. At the current price, I would recommend it. However, if you are after a game that is going to be done soon, or prefer not to be patient and see the development process through, I suggest looking elsewhere. This game has a lot of potential ahead of it, and while a lot of setbacks have overcome the developers, I am sure that given time they will make something very playabe, very decent, and very fun.

I was intrigued by the description of Analogue: A Hate Story. It's been my first encounter with visual novel and I didn't know what to expect. At first there was only confusion caused by too many characters to remember but with every log I read the story became more clear. I have to admit, I've never felt that uncomfortable playing a game.
Unusual story. I'd recommend the game, especially if you are a visual novel fan.

The basic gameplay is pretty good but the pacing is terrible. I doubt the developers played through their own tutorial. You get a short video when a decent item description would have done the job. Rather than encouraging players to explore, the game assumes the player is a moron and tells you exactly what to do, step by step for the first 3 levels. That is in addition to the pop-up tutorials every 20 feet. If you think the gamers will be too stupid to figure out your game, maybe the solution is to make the mechanic more intuitive, not have 2 dozen videos explaining various concepts peppered in waypoints.
The game does get more challenging and fun later on but the interface remains clunky. The game is plagued with interface issues: you can undo traps but not work, the hud favors artistic flare to actually providing information (health bar most guilty), you have to navigate through a half dozen buildings in town for upgrades and items, even though it could have easily all been fit into a single interface.
The game lauds it's exciting and epic story. Yet aside from an awesome opening cinematic, the game chooses to tell the story in laughable animations. They are poorly dialogued, occur much too frequently and worse, doesn't inform or drive gameplay at all. They break up the pacing of the game and most of the characters are one dimensional. Instead of a handful (yes more than 1) of animations every level, a cinematic every 5 would have been amazing.

I strongly suggest not purchasing Prototype 2. Yes, it was fun. Yes, it was marginally well-designed. But over-all, the first one was much, much better. I'll explain why, and you can decide for yourself if my issues are overriding factors for you:
1. Graphics
Prototype 2 wins. I'll give it that. It's gorgeous. Poorly optimised, so you're gonna get a crap framerate, but it's gorgeous.
2. Control scheme
Prototype 1 takes the gold there. P1's controls are well-mapped by default and make sense once you become aquainted with them. P2 changes some core controls for no reason, and because of the way they're set up, rebinding them will not help.
3. Movement and parkour systems
P1 wins, but mostly because of the control setup. It just flows better, not only because it's been designed better, but also because the controls don't appear to have been designed for a race of crab people.
4. Gameplay
P1 and P2 are actually somewhat tied gameplay-wise. P1's open-world is far more enjoyable and feels more "alive." Things do NOT despawn. I don't mean like they don't despawn for a long time, I mean they DO NOT. I once, to test it, hijacked a helicopter and left it on a roof down on the south end of the map. I then spent an hour or so screwing around in the north end of the map. I then returned and found my chopper in the exact state I had left it, ready for me to board.
NPCs react semi-realistically. Civillians will run in fear and panic if they see you changing state, military personell can be fooled enjoyably with shape-shifting, and overall the NPC life feels "alive."
P2 wins in events and missions. P1 ultimately has the story missions and that's it. There are side-missions but they're boring as hell and are repetitive, with no real incentive to play them. Granted, it makes up for it by having an enjoyable open-world to explore, but it fails to encourage playing the events. P2, however, has better mission design, even if it does get a little repetitive, and incentive is given in the form of power upgrades to play through the side-missions.
Things despawn BADLY. I found two NPCs sitting on some chairs and rotated the camera. When it was turned back, they were completely different races and genders. Vehicles left lying around will disappear as soon as your field of view is broken by buildings.
NPCs have slightly better animations but don't react well. Fooling military personell feels like I'm playing hide-and-seek with a babysitter. "Where's the horrifying shapeshifting abominaattiooooonn? I can't fiiiiind hiiiim. Is he heeeere? How about in heeeere?" It just gets old quickly.
5. Story
P1's story is far, far superior, and not just because P2 suffers from sequelitis. P1's story is about a man put in confusing circumstances finding out his horrifying past and learning to live with it while being targetted by a shadow mega-corporation that has accidentally caused the destruction of New York. P2's story is about a man finding out his just-for-heart-string-tugging family has been murdered going up against a Saturday morning cartoon villain. To make it worse, P2's main villain is the protagonist of P1, the man you've come to be attached to, and ultimately see as a hero, despite the horrors he's been forced to commit. It feels like a cheap twist placed in for no particular reason other than the writers needing a way to not make you the P1 protagonist again.
6. Overall experience
I enjoyed Prototype 2 but only in a very brief sense, about as long as the story lasted, and not for the story, for the missions. While both games offer new-game+ experiences, I just couldn't bring myself to do it with P2. It felt like funding had been cut after the missions had been basically designed, leaving a programmer to write the story and a modeller to design the open-world. Compared to Prototype 1, where I'm currently on new-game+ number four, I just can't recommend Prototype 2. It's fun for a day and that's the end of it, versus fun for as long as you're creative.

Yes. Yes. And a million times: YES!
Delivered by the developers of the probably most controversial game "Hatred" comes their newest work: IS Defense.
So what is it about? In case you haven't noticed already, the game is set in a unreal (yet scaringly possible) future where ISIS has taken over north Africa and is starting an offensive against Europe. Your job is to stop them, one Bullet at a time...
(TL;DR in the end)
First things first, I don't like rail shooters. I don't like them at all. But this game does not feel like a rail shooter, more like a first-person tower defense, and it's totally AWESOME!
Your only task in the game is to pop some Jihadists. How? It's up to you.
Unlike other railshooters (even though I won't count IS Defense as one) you don't just click with your cursor across the screen, instead you're placed on a stationary fortificated hill with a Machine gun (unlimited ammo, but magazine size of 200 shots) and a Bazooka (you start with 6 shots, you get more via supply drops, I'll get to them later), which can turn around 360 degrees.
Along with your weapons, you are given a variety of point streaks (Supply drop, Infantry support, Artillery support, Air support and Helicopter support). They are all feeding from the same score pool, that means if you call in a support, you will maybe not be able to call in a different one.
While you're mowing down the islamist invaders, you gain XP, which gives your character level ups. At each level up you get one point, which can be spent in your skill tree (4 branches: Player, Machine gun, Rockets, support), which works like most other skill trees (get the lower skills to unlock higher ones, the higher ones cost more points).
The game is really hard in the beginning, but the more games you play, the stronger your character gets, the easier the game gets. Then you unlock the next map, which is harder and requires you to rank up higher to beat it etc.
I've only played the first 2 maps yet and I have to say that the developers did great work with them. I was expecting the maps to be the same with just a different look, but they aren't. While the first map is an open beach, the second map is a harbor. Where the first map was feeling hard first because of the wide field the enemies were approaching from, you will miss this wide open field in the second map. The enemies rush out of several buildings, stand on the roofs and rush around the corner with their armored cars (yes, they don't just have Toyotas with Machine guns).
The enemies vary from regular infantry, infantry with rocket launchers, suicide bombers, Toyotas and armored cars (at least I have seen so far)
Watch out for the suicide bombers tho. They're easy to spot (red clothing, suicide belt and running directly at you without a gun continously shouting in Arabic) as long as all is chilled, but when the whole screen is full of enemies, you suddenly see a Kebab infront of your face and the game is over. Regular infantry will also throw grenades when they come close to you and run away when they're on fire. The enemy vehicles try to (and WILL) run over your infantry, watch out for them. When you shoot the driver of a Toyota while the car is in motion, the car will go loose, may run over people, crash into a building, drive into the ocean and die or just turn in circles until it explodes from the fire.
All in all, the AI is perfect.
Supply drops: A dropship will drop a crate with either health or rockets into the combat zone. Shoot the crate to get it. Upgrades increase the crate number or the contents itself (like 100% health regen).
My suggestion: stockpile your crates so you can shoot the health boxes when you need them instead of calling a drop when you're low at health and die.
Infantry support: My favourite one so far. This steak calls in a group of friendly soldiers (marked with a blue diamond) to fight the enemies. Not only do they help you get more kills, they also distract the enimes from you, giving you more time to fight more enemies, reload, etc.
My suggestion: Use as much as possible.
Artillery support: Covers the combat zone with Artillery. Impacts are random and they might (and WILL) hit your allies too. Also the standard one is really short.
My suggestion: Upgrade to the longer lasting artillery and when you use it, call in the infantry after the shelling is over.
Air support: Call in jets that nuke (not really) the combat zone. More effective but more expensive than artillery.
My suggestion: Use it when you can affort it.
Helicopter support: Calls in an attack helicopter that attacks anything hostile on the combat zone. Destroys Toyotas in the blink of a second and really takes some weight off your shoulders.
My suggestion: Use it when there's heavy enemy activity.

IS Defense,
As the name says, puts you in a defensive position behind a fictional LMG. The objective of the game is as simple as it can be entertaining. Hold your ground as long as possible.
This game is very similar to P.O.W., Operation Wolf, Vietnam Gunner, Beach Head etc.
The genre is as old as computer gaming and it hasn't lost its glory. That is, if you like those kind of games.
So what is there actually to do?
1) Take out as many targets as possible before dying.
2) By destroying targets you gain round based and persistent experience points.
3) Persistent Experience points can be used to acquire permanent upgrades.
4) Round based experience points are used to call in power ups, or allied aid through soldiers, planes, arty and helicopters.
The presentation is more than adequate.
The Sound effects and narration are good.
Final verdict:
If you're offended by the name of this game then you shouldn't be on Steam, which is a western product, in the first place.
Besides of that, IS Defense is a stationary turret defense action packed ride that delivers for its low price.

I'm a big fan of endless runners, and have been waiting for two things. One: for the genre to come to PC/Mac. Two: for there to be some innovation in the gameplay structure. Last Knight does both. This game offers good challenge, a variety of characters and enviroments, a story mode, several variants on endless mode, and a randomly-generated roguelike mode. That's a lot of gameplay, and a major step forward compared to other endless runners.
Of course, it is Early Access and, as such, a work in progress. There are some bugs, and the rogue-rider mode is incomplete. I'd like to see more characters added, maybe some that think outside of the medieval box, like a robot or a valkyrie. How about a centaur? It would also be nice if we could redefine the keys, although the default keymap works well. Other than that, I have no complaints about what I've purchased.
In summary: Last Knight is currently my favorite game on the Mac. It's well worth the 5 bucks, and even more so when it's sale.

Transitioning mobile games to PC is a fickle thing. Going from a platform primarily played in short bursts while waiting in line or for a call, to one that people tend to set aside hours of their time to play something more substantial, often leaves mobile to PC ports feeling watered down; too shallow to keep the players interest when there is so much else to play and better left on the platform they originated on. This isn't to say I'm in any way opposed to mobile games coming to PC, but the way games are approached on the two different platforms is so different that it's often hard to bring one to the other without losing something along the way.
Last Knight fits into all of this for the fact of it being an endless runner, a genre often cited to have began with Canabalt but was certainly popularized with mobile games like Jetpack Joyride and Temple Run. Toco Games aren't looking to make just another runner however. Instead, there's a clear vision at the core of Last Knight that they feel the genre has room to grow past its time waster roots into something more compelling and engrossing. Fantastic visuals are the first to sell this idea, with noticeably higher production values than you see in most games of the genre, with tons of color and visual effects making for an impressive display that really makes you feel they're onto something. Looking past the pretty graphical prowess however, the game begins to show it's not as far off from its shallow contemporaries as it would like you to think.
Though split into three modes, classic endless running, a campaign, and a still in production choose-your-own-adventure experiment, the gameplay of Last Knight is relatively the same throughout all of them. Mounting your horse and grabbing a lance, you ride through levels dodging left and right between obstacles, jumping gaps, grabbing coins, and occasionally hitting an oncoming rider off his horse. It's a traditional but perfectly solid design, whose flaws lie in how actually playing it feels.
Endless runners rely on quick reflexes, which in turns require you be able to see the obstacles in front of you in time to react to them. Last Knight fails both of these by positioning the camera in possibly the worst view it could be, creating a painfully low draw distance that barely allows you to see ahead of you at all, but certainly not enough to dodge obstacles consistently with how slowly your rider moves from side to side. It makes death feel cheap and random, like you simply got unlucky by being on that side of the screen when they through something at you you had no chance to avoid. I also found myself feeling rather seasick from the view angle, which for those often prone to motion sickness in games may make the game unplayable.
Last Knight fails again in regards to making itself a game that players want to return to. Level designs are decent when you are going through the story and only seeing each area once, but in endless mode it quickly becomes obvious how little variation there is between sections, and as a result I became bored of the mode after only a handful of runs (which for an endless runner is essentially a death sentence).
I can't recommend Last Knight for a variety of reasons, but perhaps the biggest one is that for how hard it tries, it winds up even less than the free (some would say throwaway) runners that populate mobile and flash gaming. It's impressive visuals can only do so much to hide the dull and forgettable gameplay underneath, that all the while did nothing but make me wonder why I wasn't playing any number of other games instead. I'd like to say Last Knight still has potential, that while it's still in early access it has time to be reworked and improved into something more enjoyable, but at this point and with how tightly ingrained its issues are I'm really not sure it does.

Every effort was made to try and not ruin the plot of the game throughout this review. However, no promises can be made.
***Possible Spoilers follow***
An amazing game for the price.  It is definitely unique, albeit a tad bit easy.  I started the game with Jos, although I really wanted Jack because I was hoping for more gunplay.  Changed to Jack after day 3 because it seemed a bit too easy to NOT play on the mode I had originally wanted.
Although I found the gunplay severely lacking, I still enjoyed the game.  Honestly, aside from shooting Net traps or occasionally shooting enemies as they ran up, I rarely used my gun at all.  Even sitting on bonfires, I found it more advantageous to run out, do a full combo once or twice, and then run back into the saftey zone of the warming flames.
However, when you think about it, that merges great with the historical and realistic (for a game about demons and werewolves) feel that the developers were trying to create. It wouldn't make much sense for you to be running around with a musket firing off round after round during the time period the game takes place in.
I wasn't entirely thrilled by everything in the game though.  I spent a lot of the nights just sitting around waiting on my traps to go off and still using a good chunk of my AP on cutting lumber for money.  I actually found myself purposefully letting enemies get to my buildings each wave so I would have something to do.  If you understand how the traps work, you could literally clear almost every wave with traps alone.
Overall the combat system itself was poorly made.  You get your "autoattack" consisting of left clicking up to 3 times for a combo (and with your stamina thats about 6-8 clicks until you fatigue) or rightclicking to spend your "rage" points. Once you learn the system its pretty childish.  Left click combo (3 clicks) to knock an enemy down, run / sprint in circles (run around and only sprint when they get close to avoid attack), and then combo again and repeat. Throw in an occasional Right-Click for a stamina-free attack/knockdown here and there. Doing this you could take on Wendigos and The Invisible Beast no problem. After around days 3-5 I never found myself using the roll (spacebar) except during fights with the "Fireflies". There was just no point in wasting all that stamina when a quick sprint away would dodge most if not all attacks and leave you with a lot more stamina.
The "Fireflies" were probably the most annoying thing in the game.  Before you get the hang of fighting them, you will find youself constanly trying to take one down, only to find yourself slammed in the back by a fireball from another one and knocked down while the one you were fighting disappears underground to heal himself back up to full.  And thanks to the aforementioned combat system, you were really limited on your choices in fighting them with your axe.  Even once you learn how to fight them, you will still find yourself catching the occasional fireball and cursing at them.
**Small spoilers**
Which doesn't even matter towards the last few days of the game.  A very unique factor in the game was that enemies only took full damage from certain types of weapons (Normal, Blessed/Holy, or Silver).  So you had to decide what type of axe you wanted to bring with you or your types of bullets to stock up on (although as before, the gun is pretty useless unless you REALLY want to shoot something).  And then they add in THE AXE. Anyone who has played the game that far knows what I'm talking about, and others will know when they get there.
This axe does full damage to everything. EVERYTHING. So now nothing is resistant anymore.  They basically took their system and threw it out the window for the last few days of the game, making the game even easier when it was supposed to be getting harder.  After you get the axe any combat is cake.  Wendigo? No problem (although a ballista will take it out in 1 shot with the skill point). I wouldn't recommend fighting a Wendigo hand-to-hand (because they cannot be knocked down, only backwards), but it is still pretty easy. And the Fireflies become cake. 15 Health? Kinda annoying to fight when they're resistant and can heal.  After the axe they go down in about 4 or 5 swings.
**End Small Spoilers**
A lot of the traps become obsolete later on as well. The wolf trap (20 AP and some money) is all well and good early on for insta-killing 1 wolf. Later on when the wolves come in packs of 3 there is little point to it. I put 1 point in trapping just so it would hold things (mainly Maikkans) for 10 seconds so I could set a spike trap and wait for more enemies to run up on the one stuck in place. Spike traps were better for the wolves because at 55 AP they save you AP and you can set them on the spawn point to drop the packs as soon as they zone in. The hanging nets become pretty much useless unless you want to use it on fireflies, and even then since it spreads the damage around between the enemies underneath you have to run up and finish them off.  I found that setting a Cross under a net, shouting, activating cross when they got near, letting it do some damage, and then dropping the trap was the best way for clearing a group of fireflies with minimum effort. And bonfires were pretty much useless because, as I mentioned earlier, you could get through almost every wave in the game without really having to fight anything if you set your traps right.
**Small Ending Spoiler**
And the ending itself was just, bleh.  There was no real feeling that you had finished the game.  It just ends like any other day in the game. There was no big feeling of triumph after you had finished it. It ends on a definite cliffhanger, but for the time put into the game the ending just isnt there. You get like 30 seconds of cutscene or so like you would any other day of the game.  You don't even reunite with the brother whose soul you saved. Everything was building up to you defeating this super demon and saving the village, you defeat it, and then thats it. A small cutscene, and its over.  Nothing about saving the village, saving your sister, saving your brother, nothing. It just ends, and rather poorly at that.  I even found myself googling the ending afterwards to see if I had missed something.
**End Ending Spoiler**
But all of that aside, there was something about the game that compelled me to finish it.  It could have been the gamer in me that didn't want to leave a game I had bought unbeaten. It could have been the uniqueness of the game itself.  But everything aside, I did find the game very enjoyable for the price and would recommend people to pick it up. Some people may want to wait to pick it up on sale (I got mine on sale) because although $15 for the game isnt a bad price at all, the game DOES lack a certain polish that would make it a must-have. I would definitely recommend that it at least gets placed on your wish list and for you to pick it up at some point, because it is definitely a unique and intriguing game even with the flaws in the game itself.
I would like to see a sequel made, but the developers are really going to need to flesh it out a lot more to make it worthwhile, and the story is going to need to have some major work put into it. It felt like it was just a side thought to the game to spice it up a little bit in between the repititive nightly routine the game falls in to.

Story: The story takes a back seat in this game to guns and more guns. But really gameplay and coop was the main focus, with the story there to provide entertaining situations. To be honest I don't have a great recollection of what the plot was... it never really stuck with me but it didn't bother me or seem out of place. That being said they could really get away with whatever they want because the game doesn't take itself seriously at all. I'd say some of the missions have memorable bosses like slege and krom, who I enjoyed facing off with. Other than that, you're a vault hunter hunting a vault. On your way you kill lots of things. Plot summed up.
Gameplay: I like it! But don't love it. The gun-play is pretty satisfying with headshots looking sick. Your player moves nice and fast but seems sluggish when jumping or changing directions, not terribly though. The gun options and types are pretty vast and I liked most of the damage categories. I just wound up using the same op weapon for 10 levels until I found another. Not until the end game did I actually have multiple viable guns. The main way you interact with game world is talking to npcs and receiving missions. Now the missions are very mixed bag... lots of them are fetchy to death. Sometimes I'd look at my missions log and see fetch quest after fetch quest. They really feel insignificant to, with no plot or interesting reward. It just looks like these items were scatter-shot across the map, just so you would explore the whole map. On the other side of things, some missions have more plot significance and have you walking up to the front door of a bosses stronghold and blasting your way through. This straight forward action was good fun and could be challenging.
DLC: I can't recommend any of the DLC's outside of the armory. The others look and feel under-developed, with boring mission after boring plot points in uninteresting areas. And the map design seems horrible here! I found myself running doing nothing for hours in these maps.The armory on the other-hand has vehicles! Thank goodness! Also you get a ♥♥♥♥-ton of great weapons. I feel like this DLC focused on the good aspects of the original game, while the others amplified the annoying aspects.
Overall: I'm pretty neutral on this game. I'll recommend it for coop play and for those you can easily skip stupid missions and achievements without it bothering you. Expect fun gun-play and some goofy, outlandish settings and characters that you'll hopefully not get sick of too fast.

Great concept, interesting lore at the very start, love the steampunk genre... then there is all the other stuff.  Overly flashy fight markings that dumb down to aimbotted button mashing. Lack of challenging content, with AI questing that seems quite weak. Limited exploration and growth make this a game to log inot and play for half an hour when all your other game servers are full.

Presentation
The game is divided in three forms: The cut-scenes, which are nicely represented by beautiful art in 2D, as if you were reading a book, the strategy part of the game which is represented by a map in which u have a 360 degree view of the terrain u must defend and in which u can zoom in and out and finally the action part, in which you actually put your plan into action.  The action part is cartoonish but still very enjoyable to look at and in 3D.  If you are looking for 'Crysis' graphics, look elsewhere.  It's much more art oriented.  The music is taken from canadian folklore and is quite nice to listen to.  As for the sounds (explosions, beasts roars, axe hits, guns firing,.) they are well executed and add tangibility to the game.
Gameplay
As mentioned above, this is a mixed game, whereas you play a tower defense game at first and after that you put your plan to execution in a 3rd view action game.  In the strategy part you are presented with a comprehensive map that tells you which creature you are going to fight, their number and their headings, i e where they will attack.  It is there that you have to put up traps to stop them from attacking buildings and thus destroying them or else you fail the scenario.  You have complete control on which traps to use, and where to use them (as long as they are unlocked from progressing in the game).  You are only limited by the in-game mechanics, i e money and action points.
The second part is as said putting your plan into execution, and this is done by pressing the 'Start the night' button in the map view.  You then have control of a lumberjack armed with an axe an a rifle and equipped with potions.  This part is rendered in 3D with a 3rd perspective aspect.  The controls are responsive and the animations are well done.  You can view in real time your traps, set them off if needed to and coming to life.  In all my gameplay, i have encountered one bug related to a specific trap, the spike trap.  Sometimes even if i was standing outside the spikes, they would hit me anyways and kill me with the other beasts standing on it.  Othe than that the gameplay is fun and sometimes even scary!
Conclusion
For a 6 member studio, this game is remarkably well done.  I encountered no bugs and everything worked as described.  Depending how much time you wanna spend in the strategy map, this game should take between 10 to 20 hours to complete.  The game is not without cons, and personally i have 2.  First one is regarding the resolution.  Maybe the Devs will patch this up but for now the highest resolution is 1080P.  Second con, if they would also patch the icons in the 3D view which are not big enough with higher resolutions.  Other than that i highly recommand this game.

I've played two of these types of games now (although this is set in some form of futuristic Korean ship rather than Japan), and am struck by the similarities. There's always one chick who's pretty, cute, subservient, likes geeky things. Then she has a sister/friend/nemesis who has an 'attitude', a kooky sense of style and is independent - the hard to get one. Yet one or both randomly and suddenly fall in love with you with equal ease despite not knowing you and it being ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED that you're a loner who is awkward in the outside world and avoids people. Oh, and the women in this game are AI, so NOT EVEN REAL OR PHYSICALLY ABLE TO INTERACT WITH YOU.
The reason I mention this is I thus fully expected this to be written by a guy who has projected himself as the main character, but actually it was written by a woman, a self-proclaimed feminist, and the main point was that it was supposed to bring awareness to the horrible things women in Korea a couple of centuries back had to live through. So I don't get why I'm wanting to bang the AI or why she felt the need to dress it up with this flirty subplot. I guess this is what these kinds of games all do, given my limited experience, but there's nothing wrong with breaking the mould.
There are some interesting mini-stories told via the diaries and emails you snoop, written well enough. So I do recommend this game if this all sounds normal to you. You're probably used to it by now. If it's your first foray into this mad world of awkward Japanophile virgins, it's worth a look too since the world there once was on this ship is kinda interesting.

In the game you are equipped with a glove that has up to 5 slots for shooting a glowing orb. These orbs are used to lock, unlock the flow of energy to doors and lasers. You can also use the orbs to build platforms on what looks like oil(it's a black liquid) to traverse areas in rooms. The jumping in this game is fantastic(and required) because each jump is scary due to the fact there are no checkpoints or quick saves. And what would a puzzle game be without picking up and placing a block on a button?
There are 22 rooms to solve and most are not very difficult except maybe the final two rooms where it's more tension(jumping) than the difficulty of the puzzle. The one new system SolarGun does present is when you die your glove is suspended from the ceiling with 3 lines at the point of death(Max of 3). It's a neat idea and could have been trouble if it had more weight but it easily was just a distraction in some areas where you will die a few times. Speaking of dying, there are two insane achievements for the game. One is no death and another for finishing the game in 25 minutes. Both to me would require a LOT of practice and playthroughs, a LOT.
I believe i would call myself a veteran of puzzle games. I play them a lot and while SolarGun is familiar, like a lot of games today, it's always fun to revisit even if it for just a brief time. I spent close to 2.5 hours to complete the game and it's easy to recommend and an absolute steal, literally, at .89.
Played the game on my MSI ApachePro 1080P max settings 60+ frames with zero problems.
Positives
Absolute steal for the price

Looks good, ran fantastic

Unique death idea for the genre

Solar gun is a short but entertaining First Person Puzzle game. The player is a female character with tidy nails and a gauntlet that can shoot energy orbs into switches to activate them, or into water to create a platform. Other gameplay elements include "weighted cubes", pressure plates, switches to on/off lasers, scissor elevators and many kinds of catwalks for the platforming aspect of the game.  Speaking of which, jumping physics can  be awkward until you get used to it.
As mentioned, it's short. It can be completed in less than 25 minutes (there is an achievement for this) once you learn the puzzles. Maybe an hour in the first run. That's because the puzzles, while fun and we'll plotted, are fairly easy.
Graphics are minimalistic, relying on a simple palette of blues, yellows and greys, all solid colours with some sort of film grain on them. Well suited for this kind of games.
There's plenty room for improvement when it comes to music, as it is too low and somewhat dull.
Once you finish the game you can test your skills in the bonus maps or try a no-deaths run or a speedrun.
If you are into first person puzzle games, I recommend Solar Gun. Worth the price.

After playing this game for four hours--unable to stop myself until after I've progressed to Chapter 3, I can safely say that I REALLY enjoy this game. And that's coming from someone who does NOT like playing Fighting Games, I have a temper problem with getting hammered into the ground constantly and I have slammed my controller onto my table in a fit of rage once whilst playing this game but I can safely that was that due to the computer being a cheap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and not so much my skill being obsolete! =P
The combat is VERY fluid and feels nice, the enemy will always adapt to the way you play.. if you beat on their face a lot they're going to teleport away a lot, if you hang at a distance and pelt them with ranged weapons they burst their way towards you to beat your face in. If you hammer them constantly with jutsu, they'll start blocking and dodging at the last second. Sometimes you have to alter your strategy on the fly and find ways to counter them, I've lost more than a few fights already and it's never a pleasant feeling when you 'DGAF' button gets pressed.
Story is pretty solid and makes you feel as if you're actually PLAYING the anime, not the game and draws you in. The pacing is perfect, the controls feel marvelous on my controller and it's not overly complicated like most fighting games tend to be. There IS no Right, down, circle down to right, b then wait 2 seconds then hit Y. It's just charge up, tap this button, now wait and avoid attacks and hit this button and BLAMMO, combo initiated. For that reason alone, I love the combat system. It's something that even a casual gamer like myself can enjoy. The difficulty of the story is unable to be altered, and the enemies scale in difficulty based on who you're fighting and how serious they're taking you, and if you lose to them too many times the game lowers their difficulty so you CAN beat them and progress so there's no wall blocking your progress.
You get rewarded for completing bonus objectives which are a lot of fun to do, especially when you finally land that specific requirement and can actually see what your new reward is! I tend to average either A's or S' for my ranks after defeating somebody, and it's very gratifying to see that high rank consisently. I honestly can find NOTHING wrong with this game, personally, and for that reason alone I'm giving this game a 10 out of 10. A must-have for ANY Naruto fan... though if you've never seen the end of the Series leading UP to Shippuden? You're probably going to be confused about a lot of things.
