Eve is not a game. It is pretty much an alternate universe. Eve is an ever-changing 24-7 world of politics and warfare, with you caught in the middle. The game starts with the new tutorial I haven't done. But it teaches you the controls. That's it. Everything else is up for you to learn. (just kidding, you look it up) Your life starts very peaceful, but from there you are at the steering wheel for what you want to do, and it is overwhelming. This is the stage people usually quit. They can't handle it. Don't. The moment you get over this hump this game will become your second life. This game has something for literally every player. There has to be something you like. Like exploring the unknown? Take an explorer frigate and go deep into wormhole space. Want to craft? Make billions by running your own industry startup. Want to slowly hate every other player in Eve? Mine. Want to PvP? Blob up with your friends and go destroy some poor guy's ship. Or do honorable 1v1 duels. Want to scam people out of all their money? You can do that too. Eve is a dangerous world. You will die. A lot. Even the best pilots die. Your ship is gone, and now your capsule is gone. Don't worry, you come back as a clone of yourself, ready to do it all over again. If you really want to get the most out of eve, you need to learn that death is a game mechanic.
Eve Online has captured me like no other game. World of Warcraft? I love that game, but the moment I picked up eve I neglected it. The game sucked me in, and it will suck you in too, if you let it. So hit that "play game" button, and bring some open-minded friends. Or make your own. The game is all about having your friends and your own little corperation, begging to do something big. To change Eve forever in the vast political landscape. I recommend joining some nullsec corp (you'll learn what that is when you play) and having your own little safe pocket in the universe surrounded by your friends. This review is a mess, but my heart basically just spilled out onto the keys. Eve is my favorite game of all time, and it can be yours too. But don't download it on steam. Please, please don't download it on steam. Download it on the official website for gods sake. Steam integration sucks so bad. So, what I'm trying to say with this review, is play this game.

A refreshing take on tower defense strategy with with a supernatural theme. Nice musical scoring, sound effects and a decent albeit simplistic storyline makes it more believable and immersive. It's quite addictive once you get into it. It's kinda short but I think has some decent replay value as the game's many traps, weapon types, magical artifacts and terrain based tactics provide for alot of flexibility and different approaches to progressing through the levels. There is also of course a fairly typical multi-branch skill tree that lets you develop your style however you want.
You basically plan your strategy and setup your traps during the day and then execute it at night, the object being to survive and make it to the next night, which progressively gets more difficult. There are many areas of the map that need defending, so careful planning, timing and execution are essential. And the devs of course left the ending wide open for a sequel which I can say I'm looking forward to. Definitely worth picking up on sale.

First, the bad news. The first time you do a (level 10?) dungeon (PER character), expect the game to lock the dungeon reward screen on you to the point you have exit out of the game. Near as I can tell, this only happence once per character. For good or bad, you get 5 characters per account. Any server you log into will show any characters you have already made.
The game is sometimes hard to log into. They seem to be working hard on content and bugs. I got fairly quick responses to the emails I sent to them, and have edited and kept this review updated accordingly.
Next, the good news. Its actually worth dealing with bugs till they fix it.  My husband and I discovered this game on the same day, and as we played, it seemed every 10 minutes or so we were finding something new that we loved about the game. I haven't seen him this hooked in a loong time.  I've paid it the highest compliment I know how for a game... I created a solo... I almost never solo.  Yeah, its that much fun. If you like steampunk at all, you want to give it a shot.
Yes, the character creation is exceedingly limited, and the classes *seem* limited. Trust me, by level 6 or so you dont care. The classes have variations within them. And the looks of the character constantly develop in game, given a combination of luck and your taste.
They are generous with rewards for those who log in every day for up to seven days in a row, and have a constantly changing event giving out new rewards simply for being logged in and playing on any given day. Almost everything you do has a completion reward, collection reward, something extra built into it. It may sound overwhelming, but give yourself a day and you will find that they did an excellent job of helping you track it. While it may seem too easy at first, you really come to  appreciate their ingenious ways of helping you to track as you level up and find more to keep track of.
Now something that some will see as horrible and others as excellent... I happen to love it. This game reaches new heights in pitting brain vs brawn. If all you do is push to level up to max in one weekend, you could find yourself with a level 50 character with little better than level 10 abilities. Every time I play I find new ways they give to make your character unique. There are miriad ways to buy, build, plan, level everything about your character, and every level counts. Each time you finish your quest and level up, take the time to look around, did you do your dailies and level up your abilities? Do you spend more on your merc(battle pet, in essense) or more on your armor, or more on your abilities? Do you buy more bag space or a better buff pet? All choices are good, and all take time to build.  If you love to do a slow, thorough build of your character, like I do, you will find this game addictive. If you are all about the max level as fast as possible, you may find yourself a little frustrated with having to slow down and plan your character. Either player type given time can find themselves addicted to this game.
Hope this review helps. Keep up the good work!

I purchased the spearhead edition of this game when it was largely new, but my poor laptop could not run it. Now that I have a powerful tower, I am able to actually enjoy this game. What I like best about the game is the atmospheric settings that sold me on it in the first place. wheather the map is on space or planetside, they find ways to greatly shift how the area feels and looks, be it with power failures leaving you with blaring red lights (or pitch black darkness), or several weather effects like fog, heavy rain and thunder.
As far as difficulty goes, there is certainly no want for a greater challenge, as even the normal difficulty will give an unprepaired player a difficult time. The hard an realistic difficulties are for use with other players and friends for sure. You could probably draw similarities between this game and other "real" tactical shooters like SWAT and such, where you need to know when to move carefully but deliberatly. The easy mode works fine, as its still very possible to lose if you are foolish.
Because the game is in early access, there is an issue with the variety of enemies,  there are two basic types at the time of this review, both are humanoid combat androids. One variant is armed with the same basic guns you use, the other charge at you and attempts to pumble you to death (with surprising efficiency). Although this might seem rather lacking, the two work fantastically with each other, particully in the lighting restricted environments. If you keep your flashlight on to keep from being run down and ambused, you'll easily draw the attention of a gun weilding bot, but if you become to reliant on always sticking to the dark, you'll be in for quite a shock when one comes sprinting out of the darkness right in your face.
With that talk of darkness, the game does have a pretty well fleshed out stealth system, with variable walk speeds, crouch speeds, and sprinting all causing different levels of noise, which can and WILL attract the attention of the enemies. You can use this, along with the darkness and a silencer to avoid and even ambush enemies. Many environments have lights you can shoot out for more cover, at the cost of being harder to see enemies. The shifiing weather and daytime also affects howe hard it is for them to see you. At this time, I cannot tell if the camo patterns you can select for your armor and gear have any effect on visability.
So long as you have a rig strong enough to run it, this is a great in-progress title. The devs may be moving a little slow, but I like whats been done so far, and I'm glad to see the game hasn't been abandoned.
I would recomend this game, especially if you have friends to play it with.

I'm going to be honest...I kind of liked this game, at the start. Steampunk and fantasy, what could go wrong? And at the start, it was quite fun, seemed like good story...until you get to Arkadia.
It doesn't take long for the game to get repetetive. In fact, to level up all you need to do is log into the game and claim daily prizes, that's about it. Fighting is routine, just mash hordes of monsters. As a player of MMOs such as Dungeons & Dragons Online and The Lord of the Rings Online, I had high hopes for City of Steam.
Alas, while it was cool in the beginning...it gets boring once you get to the main city in the game. There's not much storyline after the intro, and you can't do much in the way of exploring. The races are balanced, the concept of the game is very promising...but if you're intending on playing it past the intro, I can't suggest it. All it's good for in the end is going into a dungeon and killing hordes of bugs and mechanical annoyances, which aren't that hard to beat. Even the bosses are easy to take down. As a player of MMOs, I was hoping for more actual fighting and...well, being able to explore the world.
As much as I wish I could, I can't recommend this game. Does the story show promise? Yes. Could the game have been more than it is? Yes. The sad part is the developers didn't take that route, and City of Steam: Arkadia seems like it's vastly unfinished in terms of story and exploration.

I tend not to like puzzle games that much, but I quite enjoy Solargun. I enjoy the puzzles lot, with the mechanics being interesting and intuitive.The developers also spend the a large amount of time making the lab feel like it was actually used, which I really like.
A large number of the puzzles can be quite challenging and require some platforming skill. However, the platforming can be problematic at times, which is a shame. The character you control is feels rather heavy, meaning you carry a large amount of momentum. While not itself problematic, it makes air control difficult, making precision platforming a pain at time. Another part that can be annoying is the death marker, which while funny because of the whole "save the equipment, not the person" joke, they can easily get in the way of platforming because they are physical objects. There are also some other small complaints, such as lack of options in the settings, (sensitivity, keybindings, resolutions) and the artstyle making stuff look fuzzy.
Overall, I enjoy it quite a bit. I think all of the puzzles are fun and unique, the lab an interesting place and the mechanics of the Solar Gun well implemented.  The vast majority of the problems are fairly minor and can be overlooked, even though the physics can be annoying at times. So, if you like puzzle games and have some spare change in your steam wallet, I would definetly pick this up, because it is worth every penny.

As others have said (and as you can see for yourself) this is a first person puzzle platformer in the same vein as Portal and The Talos Principle.
Visually, this is a good looking game and the environment reminds me of portal. It's mostly a futuristic industrial setting with some random rooms that look like parts of an office building. Most of the rooms are pretty minimalistic. Overall it's a pretty clean aesthetic.
The puzzles aren't very difficult or complicated. If you've played through Portal or Talos, these will be a breeze. (But they're still fun.) Only a few of them require you to time your moves just right, but several require accurate jumps. Nothing super frustrating, though. I completed the game in about an hour.
As for the puzzles themselves, most of them revolve around little energy orbs that you can shoot (in limited quantities) from your hand. You can also reclaim these orbs if they're no longer needed. There are also the staples of the genre such as killer pools of liquid, lasers, switches, and (of course!) the generic cube/box.
If you're looking for a story, I'm sorry to say that you won't find it here. There's no text or dialog in the game. It's obvious that there's some sort of back story here, but they don't really put any effort into telling you what it might be. There are various office building type rooms scattered around as well as rooms that look like experiments have taken place in them, but you're really left to make up the story on your own. It's all vaguely reminiscent of Portal.
All in all, I definitely recommend the game if you're into the first person puzzle genre. It's a good deal for the $0.99 I paid.

I like this game, it follows the One Piece manga story to a T.  The game will run all the way until Luffy meets Brook and Nico Robin. Sadly, the gameplay is rather repetitive and plays like Sangoku Mushi. You could even call this Koei Tecmo's One Piece reskinned Sangoku Mushi. Personally, I would have preferred Darksider II, Devil May Cry instead with Luffy being able to grapple onto different things. This isn't a AAA game but it's still fun to play. I liked it mostly because of the One Piece sauce. Supposedly, this is the PS3 port not the PS4 port so some things might be missing. The game ends at the Dressrosa Arc after you defeat Doflamingo.
Conclusion, try this game if you enjoy the One Piece manga or the Sangoku Mushi style of gameplay. Be prepared to be disappointed by the repetitiveness and the Dream Log.
1. One Piece Sauce
It's the theme that attracts me the most. Oda Eiichiro's One Piece manga is the main draw of this game.
2. Oars Battle at Thriller Park
It was the one time that the camera perspective changed and you could fight a big♥♥♥♥♥monster.
1. Repetitive Sangoku Mushi Gameplay
It's exactly like Sangoku Mushi with the Musou powers. Kill a bunch of creeps, kill a high level guard, kill the boss. Rinse and repeat.
2. Interrupting Cut-Scenes
As much as I like the story, I hate the cut-scenes appearing in the middle of a fight.
3. Music from Marvel vs Capcom
Couldn't you have made an original score from the anime?
4. Oars Battle Changing
I hated running back and forth around the courtyard just to hit Oars the same way.
5. Missing Characters
Tontoros, Capone Bege, Jewelry Bonney, Uroge, X Drake, Basil Hawkins, Eustass Kid, Scratchman Apoo,  Viola (Current Crown Princess), Scarlett (Former Crown Princess), Rebecca, Kyros, Tank Lepanto. These are just a few names missing from the game.
6. Sudden Loss Mechanism
The game is designed to force you to lose abruptly at certain points of the game. I find that to be extremely lousy game design. At the very least, try to fake it the reason for the loss.
7. End of the Dream Log
Disappointing. I was hoping you would put in a special character like Sengoku, Dragon, or Kaido. Sadly, the Dream Log is just a mass battle with the crew of the Straw Hats in pairs followed by a final battle with all 8 members at once.
1. Less Sangoku Mushi style fights
I'm extremely bored with the reskinned Sangoku Mushi style fights. I was hoping for more Devil May Cry/Nier Automata/God of War/Darksiders kind of gameplay where there is a special boss who has special attack patterns to decipher.
2. Create NPCs exclusive to the game
Mr 10, Miss Tuesday. These guys don't appear in the manga. Create exclusive scenarios for them in the game.

Eve Online is perhaps the all time worst game for instant gratification seekers. It is neither intuitive nor simple. The game mechanics are byzantine. This is a sim for players who want to get lost in a thriving sandbox that is shaped by the efforts of the player base. Eve is deep, challenging, beautiful, and life-devouring. It continues to stand as the high water mark for sandbox game design's potential for player-driven content, emergent economics, and high stakes PVP warfare on a truly galactic scale. To see why this sandbox is surviving through the devoted investment of time and effort of a cult-like player base, stick with it. Your success depends on forethought and awareness. Lazy and impatient players will suffer. Learn from your failures or you will rage-quit like a child. Patient and adaptive players will carve out niches for themselves and leave their mark on the game world. Whether you are a devoted team player or a con artist sociopath, the social aspects of this game are absolutely key. Join an active nullsec corp. Get on Teamspeak. Veteran pilots tend to love to show rookies how to thrive, and mentorship is the best way through the steep learning curve. If you merely fly solo in High Security space, you'll remain stuck in the shallow end of Eve's potential. This is not a design-and-dump product. Hardcore Eve pilots know exactly why flashier younger spaceship sandbox games still don't pose a threat to the survival of Eve Online. Those games can never lay claim to Eve's core legacy: years of elite player ambition, investment, and struggle that makes a tangible difference in the game world.

Due to a minor adjustment needed to fix the FPS glitch given to me by steamuser Reanimate (thank you by the way)  I reassessed my review and I recommend although I will still leave my old review untouched below:
**INITIAL OLD REVIEW (OBSOLETE)**
Don’t get me wrong, I have high praise for; and have thoroughly enjoyed Dead Island (700+ hours in game speaks for itself I think).  And when I found out they were optimizing and overhauling one of my favorite zombie games I was excited.  And I was even more excited to find out that I would be receiving it at a discounted price for owning the original release.
And upon playing Dead Island: Definitive Edition I was very impressed at first, but that all changed when I hit the city of Moresby and had FPS drops in the rate of 25 to 35 FPS which, I am sorry to say this, but that is inexcusable especially for a seemingly ‘Definitive’ revamp of the title.
Now it is under my understanding that this game was overhauled using Dying Lights engine.  And it shows very much because the look and feel of Definitive Edition definitely resembles Dying Light in some aspects which is good I think.  But the main reason I bring this up is because Dying Light runs perfectly fine on my PC and is a more newer game with bigger open worlds, so I do not see any justification in why a revamped 5-year old game (which is smaller in scale in pretty much every way to Dying Light as far as map size as well as actively visible NPC’s on screen at once to my knowledge).  Would have FPS drops in the range from 25-35 FPS for no real reason to me.

Now there is a slight (very slight) chance this maybe just my PC but I think otherwise.  I expected this ‘Definitive Edition’ to be defined in mostly every way performance and graphical wise (as hinted) to Dead Island original.  As for now, I cannot give this game a thumbs up rating until they improve upon optimization.  That being said, I still think Dead Island is one of the best zombie games of its genre made (with Dying Light being its overall better successor for its genre).

This marks my first steam review and on a game that I've played extensively to boot. I'll get right to the point, this game is very two-faced in int's pros and cons. On one hand if you're an old fan of the dragon Ball Series this sort of RPG/Beat 'em up gamestyle will feel very nostalgic and rewarding. On the other hand the game suffers significant online play issues that can seriously kill the expoerience if you like engaging in PvP. I will not get into huge detail on the game mechanics themselves but rather highlight some of the main high and low points that have both kept me hooked, and have somewhat drained my interest.
First off the main pro of the game: Character customization. You can choose a number of cosmetic features to make your player look the way you want. Far from perfection, but a big plus. You can also change out the move sets on the fly and as you acquire more moves you can narrow your selection to those that match your playing style best.
The con: You will find a lot of players criticize the actual game mechanics which are valid, but the chief downside to this game on the PC is that the online play was very poorly designed for handling cheaters. A cursory look at the leaderboard for ranked battle will show a number of scores that out-digit the games' ability to accurately read them. I don't know how active the online play was immediately after release but If you're looking to move your way up in the ranks the top 20 scores combined with the current inactivity of ranked effectively makes the venture pointless and unmotivating. I've run into several cheaters who have also freely used trainers and cheat engine scripts in online play to sway the outcome of pvp matches,
This cheater problem is not so much an issue for PQs at least but to do any productive PvP almost necessitates networking with other players to get a decent experience, something already pushed by the games very limited fixed chat function.
So in summary your gaming experience is going to rely heavily on your goals when you play it, and how well you can adapt to the poor handling of cheaters. The game can still be very much enjoyable withe the right people, but there are hurdles to climb in that really makes the $50 price tag on this game less than desireable. If you buy - get it on sale when its cheaper.

Since this is on sale, a short first impression: Sand-Froid has an intriguing storyline with nice athmosphere and music. The gameplay is divided into strategic planning (i.e. setting traps, managing money and action points) and fighting wolves with an axe and a front-loader rifle, ideally making strategic use of the traps you set in the previous phase. If strategy appeals to you, do not be afraid to play as Jack.
The game owes some of its mechanics to tower defense with a hero, but it transcends those in ways that give it much more flexibility and promise to make it much more interesting. That is mostly because the enemy waves have objectives and no fixed paths, and the player can influence them in various ways.
The game is fairly simple toget the hang of if you know to WASD your way around at night. I don't expect Sang-Froid to have the depth of a "serious" strategy game because this game seems aimed at the discerning casual gamer, but I'm confident that however "casual" the experience might turn out to be, it's going to be enjoyable. Recommended.

This game is terrible. If all of the negative reviews that were considered "most helpful" still hasn't convinced you not to play this game, then I shall tell you more.
The only permanent weapons are for $$$. Real money. And I'm sure some of them STILL aren't permanent. I'm not going to cover it, since a lot of reviews say it.

Next? Controls are ungodly. The devs looked at WASD and said "You know, this is great and all, but I think they'll prefer FGHT much more" or something like that. Also, your mouse is NOT the fire/aim button. So remap the keys, right? WRONG!!! I swear, they want you to use the regular keys. When i went to remmap them, i put in "WASD" as the keys selected, then I pressed "A" to move left... and nothing happened.
You have to spend a lot of time to even get the CONTROLS right. They want you to map them a certain way. The fact that it's there in your options doesn't mean it'll work in-game. Also, the options menu isn't even available during a match for some reason. And, oh, it's one of THOSE games. You know... the kind that PENALIZES YOU FOR LEAVING THE MATCH!!!!! The options aren't available in-game, so you can't re-map the keys like in any other game. You have to either A) leave the match with the penalty or B) wait the game out, THEN re-map the keys. You can modify volume and such by pressing a button the keyboard. On paper, this sounds great. But in practice? I'm assuming the devs thought they could do this instead of a... you know... in-match options menu?
Also, "E" was my use key, but when I pressed it, it didn't do a thing. Why? I don't even know.
Also, ever so long ago, like six months ago before I uninstalled this game for the first time, I lost connection to a game... that I was hosting. Ugh... It's probably fixed now, but seriously?
If you can't tell, don't get this game. The only reason you should think about installing and playing is to see how awful it is.
Oh, right, the graphics are nice in my opinion, but who cares when the game is awful?

Enemy Front is quite a good shooting game.
It's set during the Second World War, and is reminiscent of MOHAA (Medal of Honor: Allied Assault - which, by the way, was a great game; I'd love to see it on Steam).
Both single-player and multi-player game types are available.
However, multi-player is pretty much dead online, which is a shame.
I've often found that there is just one server running, courtesy of some guys who play Enemy Front on a regular basis (usually playing with an informal no-scope rule - which is okay, once you're aware of it); but there's usually no more than 3-6 guys playing. Naturally, it would be a lot more fun if there were a lot more players.
I'd suggest buying it for the single-player game; and if you get to play some multi-player games as well, then that's a bonus.
The current price tag of $30 is a bit too much (I'd suggest that it's worth about $15 or maybe $20), so if you're undecided about purchasing it, then perhaps wait and see if it goes on sale.
The gameplay style is a bit dated, like MOHAA, but if you don't mind that then buy it and have some fun.

Combos are flashy as expected. Attacks are Basic, Ranged (Charge), Special (Musou), Unique (varies based on character), and Kizuna (rage).
You have seemingly one "Musou" move except for when you're in Kizuna mode which allows more combos and a Crew based "Musou" attack.
Upgrading your characters requires both leveling from standard combat/game progress and money, and
Completing certain requirements in each levels will allow you more coins. Some of the objectives require you to earn a certain amount of (!) points from assist kills or Kizuna Rage mode attacks, somewhat like DW8XL Rage mode giving you direct XP drops.

This is a game where you clearly see it is not a triple AAA title. However you can still have fun with it in my opinion.
The singleplayer part of the game is whilst originally not mean't to be like it, the main part of the game as the multiplayer is almost completely dead and outside of times when the game is on sale or during peak hours you are lucky to even find 2 lobbies on multiplayer (both of which will most likely not be even full). The main reason for this is the poor to no success the game had as a product on launch. Due to these reasons I will be reviewing the singleplayer part of the game.
The singleplayer, whilst flawed is actually quite a lot of fun to playthrough. The graphics in the game are still decent to good looking outside of the charachter models that have not aged as well compared to the rest of the graphics. While most of the game is spent Fighting in WW2 era Warsaw the other mission areas such as the French countryside or The Snowy Norwegian areas give a neat amount of variety onto the mission areas. The game has an alright amount of weapons and everything feels good enough in my opinion. While the story is sort of interesting it is still quite pointless in general and it is mainly told to the player in multiple cutscenes that you get after beating or starting a mission. The game is quite linear but you do have the chance to explore areas to an extent to find collectibles or ammo. You might also stumble upon some mini side activities but most of these really don't effect anything in the game outside of a few of them giving achievements or some new unimportant dialogue.
Overall the game is not as bad as people tend to say but you should not go into this game thinking you are going to get great a storyline or a triple AAA experience. Whilst my review is a Recommend I can't recommend this on full price of 29.99 €/$ (or your region equivalent) as the singleplayer will only take you around 5-8 hours to beat depending on if you just rush through it or not. I personally payed only something around the line of 3 bucks for the game and anything that is 5 €/$ (or your regional equivalent, again) is a more than a good price as you will most likely get a price ratio of a buck per hour of playtime (or less than a buck per hour of playtime) depending on how much time it takes you to beat the game. Get the game from a sale if you have literally nothing else to do or if you just want to turn your brain off for some hours. otherwise it can be skipped as there are much better similar titles out there.

It's a Musou styled game.
With that said, it's one of the best I've played, second only to Hyrule Warriors.
When you first start playing the game, you only have a small handful of attacks that you can do. Stick with it and the variety opens up very quickly, with team-up attacks and all sorts of crazy, anime BS. It's extremely satisfying mowing through hordes of literally thousands of enemies with a flurry of attacks and there are SO many characters to play as.
The storyline is, as best as I can tell, a parallel for the anime, and your attitude towards that is going to determine whether or not you enjoy it.
But like most Musou games, there is a veritable cornucopia of content. If you're a fan of this game, you will probably never run out of something to do- level a character, get S-ranks on a mission, complete all the optional objectives on a certain mission, complete it on a harder difficulty... it's kind of insane how W-Force and KT keeps putting these things out at the pace that they do.
It isn't as good as Hyrule Warriors, but I won't be playing that one on PC any time soon. This is a great game in its own right- and it also has couch co-op, which is a fantastic addition, because if anyone sees you playing this they're going to want to play too.
The only really big downside I see is that the game doesn't have correct button prompts for controllers, instead it just shows colored icons for attack buttons. For the face buttons (A,b,x,y) on an xbox controller, the colors are correct, but the other buttons aren't color coded, and thus relies on trial and error for the first time you play the game. This is a minor complaint, as half an hour in the game you'll be okay with the buttons and won't even think about it anymore.
If this game looks attractive to you and you think you'll enjoy it, you absolutely will love it. Grab it, sit down and enjoy.

This marks my first steam review and on a game that I've played extensively to boot. I'll get right to the point, this game is very two-faced in int's pros and cons. On one hand if you're an old fan of the dragon Ball Series this sort of RPG/Beat 'em up gamestyle will feel very nostalgic and rewarding. On the other hand the game suffers significant online play issues that can seriously kill the expoerience if you like engaging in PvP. I will not get into huge detail on the game mechanics themselves but rather highlight some of the main high and low points that have both kept me hooked, and have somewhat drained my interest.
First off the main pro of the game: Character customization. You can choose a number of cosmetic features to make your player look the way you want. Far from perfection, but a big plus. You can also change out the move sets on the fly and as you acquire more moves you can narrow your selection to those that match your playing style best.
The con: You will find a lot of players criticize the actual game mechanics which are valid, but the chief downside to this game on the PC is that the online play was very poorly designed for handling cheaters. A cursory look at the leaderboard for ranked battle will show a number of scores that out-digit the games' ability to accurately read them. I don't know how active the online play was immediately after release but If you're looking to move your way up in the ranks the top 20 scores combined with the current inactivity of ranked effectively makes the venture pointless and unmotivating. I've run into several cheaters who have also freely used trainers and cheat engine scripts in online play to sway the outcome of pvp matches,
This cheater problem is not so much an issue for PQs at least but to do any productive PvP almost necessitates networking with other players to get a decent experience, something already pushed by the games very limited fixed chat function.
So in summary your gaming experience is going to rely heavily on your goals when you play it, and how well you can adapt to the poor handling of cheaters. The game can still be very much enjoyable withe the right people, but there are hurdles to climb in that really makes the $50 price tag on this game less than desireable. If you buy - get it on sale when its cheaper.
As much as I enjoy the game very much and would otherwise rate it positively; given my lengthy experience with it, I'm going to grade it as "not recommended". Far from the worst game ever, but it badly needs an update of some kind to block trainer users who take their infinite HP hacks into online multiplayer.

This game is essentially a simple parody of the genre of choose-your-own-adventure text-based story driven games like Champion of the Gods or Choice of Robots but features a significantly decreased word count. There are no pictures, only boxes containing text. True to the satirical style of this game, the writing is purposefully bad and the choices you get are mostly arbitrary and lead to largely arbitrary results.
If it can be said that this game has any main goal it would have to be to unlock as many endings as possible. The endings are generally stupid and nonsensical, though a few endings make references to certain movies. There are 4 game modes based on different story genres but the game is persistently nonsensical regardless no matter which genre you play.
Perhaps the biggest weaknesses of this game are that it tries too hard to be funny yet doesn't try hard enough to create a detailed satire. Once you play it a few times (which takes less than 20 minutes) the satire wears thin and the sense of humor becomes repetitive. Beyond earning a grand total of 5 possible steam achievements there seems to be little reward in continuing to unlock the game's endings.
On the upside, I suppose this game's biggest strengths are its low cost and lack of bugs. The game's consistently poor grammar prevent if from being even remotely useful as some sort of twisted teaching aid for helping ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ adults learn how to read however. No, this game is good for a few short laughs and nothing more (unless of course you are somehow an adherent of Zen Buddhism and it is your desire to be randomly slapped down or rewarded for various random actions so as to gain greater insight into the unreality of the universe. Obviously, that's not me).

Ah EVE Online...
This has to be one of the greatest and most addicting games I have ever played. Should you play it? That depends. It offers an immense world where you can be literally anyone you want because it has something for all players in all age groups from PVP, to mining, to exploring, to trading, etc... All it asks for in return is time, but if you have a headset, you will make friends while piloting some of the coolest ships around.
The game requires a time commitment, that isn't necessarily a bad thing because the game is huge so if you are across the galaxy, prepare to slow boat your♥♥♥♥♥to where you want to be. (*Learn to use jump clones efficiently to avoid this) If you have the time, try it out. The other pilots are great, don't be put off by people saying everyone in this game is toxic and trying to get over on you becasue they aren't. Many pilots will help you with information as long as you ask in a respectable manner and the ones who scam and grief are valued members of the universe. That is what makes this game great, you can be anyone. Learn to scam others, or help others, or pirate, or mine, or trade, or explore, do whatever you want just realize this game takes time to master. Literally, your skills are time based, I enjoyed this idea because they train even why you are away and it is different that most other games.
Exploration is a lot of fun in this game, to me at least, it wasn't that you were finding things no one else has found. Quite the contrary. You were finding resources like other explorers but is the fear of getting caught exciting. When you are flying a 60million isk Astero thourgh wormhole/null space with 500 million in loot, you have to be cautious but confident in you abilities. You will die in this game, it happens, but your skills will still be ther and you can always make more isk. PVP is adrenaline enducing because it is deeper than some make it out to be. It isn't merely orbiting with guns on, you have to be calculating how to counter your target/s. I enjoyed the permanent factor of your deaths, you don't just fly back to your wreck and begin again, you have to build a new ship.
So never fly what you can't afford to lose to a point. If you finally get a cruiser for mission running, don't go PVP with it because that is how you make your isk. If you make isk exploring, once you have the isk build a mirror image of you exploration ship, that way if you get blown up you can still go out and make isk. If you mine, same thing because you might get ganked in highsec by people looking for luls. This game is another world to lose yourself in, pirates exist in this world. So learn to live with them or become one.
You can make a lot of isk in this game and PLEX your account, it is doable but I don't suggest it. Pay your subscription and keep the isk for fun/pew pew. Developers need  to eat and $15 a month isn't that much if you play 15+ hours a month it comes out to $1 dollar/hour for entertainment and this game you will enjoy. You can try it out for free but I wouldn't make your final decision on that, I would pay one month and judge afterward because the game opens up with more ships.
This is becoming longer and longer but if you are looking for a good alternate life , I highly suggest this one. How to describe this Source Mod of Half Life 2...
Well first, it's quite a unique game, one that you don't see too often anymore. Purely atmospheric, with some very appealing lighting and graphics. There is little to no music in the game, leaving you walking through a quiet and somewhat eerie area. Even so, this sets a perfect atmosphere, calmly, yet it still keeps you on your nerves.
Admittedly, the story is somewhat cliché, but is still portrayed quite well. As you progress through new areas, you meet a few new people who give you small tasks that help you towards getting off of the stranded island you are on, with an unknown company blocking any outer communication. These characters are not always friendly, some attempting to kill you, just trying to survive in this perilous land. The voice actors are brilliant, bringing life to the game and to the characters they play.
The graphics in this game are, while not perfect and somewhat buggy, still quite beautiful. There were multiple occasions where I would sit there for a few minutes and gaze out into the virtual horizon, taking in the quiet beauty. The lighting used in the maps are just worthy of a comment in itself. Dark areas have a dark glow to them, while the happier, lighter areas have a nice bright tinge to them. The infected are somewhat bland, looking as though they came from Star Trek and just have glowing yellow eyes, but they don't pose a threat, they are more there to remind you of the reason that you are there.
As a total game, I found this to be quite impressive. I HIGHLY recommend this game to those with a passion for atmosphere. Considering this was made with the HL2 engine and is only the first Act of many to come, I can only wait in anticipation for the next few Acts. This game has impressed me quite a lot, with it unique atmosphere and dramatic music. As a total, this game brings back what was missing in the gaming community; Atmosphere. Modern games incorperate as much action as they can, sometimes not letting you take a break and take it all in, but this game let's you play and take it in at the same time. Very impressed with this game, can't wait for the next Acts.

It's a Musou styled game.
With that said, it's one of the best I've played, second only to Hyrule Warriors.
When you first start playing the game, you only have a small handful of attacks that you can do. Stick with it and the variety opens up very quickly, with team-up attacks and all sorts of crazy, anime BS. It's extremely satisfying mowing through hordes of literally thousands of enemies with a flurry of attacks and there are SO many characters to play as.
The storyline is, as best as I can tell, a parallel for the anime, and your attitude towards that is going to determine whether or not you enjoy it.
But like most Musou games, there is a veritable cornucopia of content. If you're a fan of this game, you will probably never run out of something to do- level a character, get S-ranks on a mission, complete all the optional objectives on a certain mission, complete it on a harder difficulty... it's kind of insane how W-Force and KT keeps putting these things out at the pace that they do.
It isn't as good as Hyrule Warriors, but I won't be playing that one on PC any time soon. This is a great game in its own right- and it also has couch co-op, which is a fantastic addition, because if anyone sees you playing this they're going to want to play too.
The only really big downside I see is that the game doesn't have correct button prompts for controllers, instead it just shows colored icons for attack buttons. For the face buttons (A,b,x,y) on an xbox controller, the colors are correct, but the other buttons aren't color coded, and thus relies on trial and error for the first time you play the game. This is a minor complaint, as half an hour in the game you'll be okay with the buttons and won't even think about it anymore.
If this game looks attractive to you and you think you'll enjoy it, you absolutely will love it. Grab it, sit down and enjoy.

This is an absolutely fantastic game - a classic of the RTS genre and it's such a shame that they never remade this game with modern graphics. If you love Star Wars or just RTS' in general, this is a game you will enjoy playing. Expect Age of Empires style mechanics and a wide variety of units designed to bring the pain. Quick note regarding the lore/canon - this game was made BEFORE Revenge of the Sith came out so the canonical sins can be forgiven (Most of the time the game simply glosses over the events of RotS anyway).
However, if you do not wish to mess around in the game files DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. It has been released in a horrific state:
1. You cannot launch it from Steam. For whatever reason, the Steam targeted executable only plays the opening movies and thats it (Workaround - simply rename 'Player.exe' to anything else and rename 'battlegrounds_x1.exe' to 'Player.exe').
2. The Clone Campaigns expansion does not work from the get-go. You have to find a patched version of the 'battlegrounds_x1.exe' online and replace the old one with it (Just search 'clone campaigns no cd patch' and grab version 1.1).
3. The music files are all missing, so there is no in-game music (menu music only). No idea whether that was deliberate or not but you can always have YouTube running whilst playing).
4. Without a widescreen patch the max resolution is 1280x720. Even with widescreen patches it's not 100% 1080p but its the best that can be done.
5. On newer OS' (I say 'newer', I mean Windows Vista and up) the DirectDraw render is bugged awfully. You need to patch the executable (again, I know) in order to get colours to work correctly (sometimes the game won't even start at all unless you patch it).
It's in a pretty poor state right now but the Discussions forums are really helpful. You shouldn't have to put in more than 10 minutes fixing time to get it to work.
Final Note: I have received reports that this game cannot be refunded for whatever reason. It's a risk you'll have to take.
So, in conclusion, this game is excellent to play but you'll need to invest your own time in order to get to that point. I do reviews based on my own experience and fun I've had already outweighs the initial tinkering I had to do to get the game to work.

The loading times for this game are insanely quick. It takes anywhere from 1 second to 2 seconds to load up the map after clicking play.
Overall, the graphics are very nice. Most of it is highly comparable to Dying Light, such as the grass, a good chunk of the textures and models, the air particles, etc.

Although the UI for Dead Island was never amazing, it could still use some improvement. In the original Dead Island the upgrade damage/force/durability was added onto the end of the original rather than just added all together. This made comparing weapons easier, and for some reason it was removed in Riptide and carried over to the Definitive Collection. The main menu also seems laggy because it's locked at 30 fps for some reason.
While most textures look great, others are lacking. The models could also be better. Although quite a few of them have been upgraded, there are some that haven't been touched or are broken. See
for specifics and screenshots.
Quite a few glitches seem to been patched, such as glitching through walls, getting out of the map and items disappearing. However, there are still some significantly big bugs present. See
for specifics and screenshots.
Most of the sounds haven't been touched other than the ladders. This means that all of the walking sound mismatching from the original is still in this one. There's also a weird audio level bug that randomly occurs when playing online, causing random sound effects to become extremely quiet.
I know Dying Light didn't have character shadows, but come on. I miss looking down and seeing my shadow moving with the derpy character animations. I don't know how many times I've just looked down and started spinning around in circles trying to find it.

I have had so many games for over 2 years and only players 150 ish hours on them. However, I've had Eve for only 6 months and already have 300+ hours on the game. Me myself I have my own whole huge story with many events that led to it. I am addicted, and here's why. (This is my first ever review so please be nice thank you! :)
Graphics:
I have a gaming PC and on best settings, it runs smooth 60. I have never experienced the game lagging and I have a GTX 770. The game looks beautiful.
Starting Up:
You can change every aspect of your characters' body. From toe length to jawline, you can move it all around, not only that, you can also choose how muscular you want your character to be and also his/her weight and much, much more.
The Game Itself:
Let's be straight forward. If you love a complicated game, this is for you. The amount of things you have to think of, all the things you need to do, how you slowly need to grow over time. This isn't a game where you leave it open and it does the work for you overnight, no, you need to work your way from a rookie ship, all the way to the biggest and baddest ship in the game. It sounds easy...but it's nowhere near it. Eve has it ALL. You can move things around, fight, mine, sell, create. So many different things.
Now the market on Eve is 100% a player made and controlled market. Anything and everything you find on sale were made by a player. Prices go up and down depending on demand. YOU MAKE THE SHIPS!! It won't be there for you, you need to make it! That is THE ONLY WAY you will be able to sell/buy/craft a ship.
Now regardless of that, there are hundreds of weapons in the game. You can't just simply buy these weapons and put them onto your ship. Each ship gives a special bonus to a type of item, mainly guns but other things too. You'll have to train skills. Yes, these skills can sometimes take days to finish, but when you finish them, you will get a very powerful ship, with an AMAZING community to teach you how to use it.
A game where war with others has POLITICS and all the smallest phrases one says can change the whole outcome of a friendship. Look at the fountain war for example.
And finally, the thing I love most...there are no restrictions. You can betray crops, spy on them, backstab them, there is no limitation to what you can and cannot do. If you have the power/skill to do it, then you can do it and no one will stop you, unless of course, they're much stronger than you. Most of the times, backstabbing doesn't happen because you'll get killed instantly but with the right plan, you can pull it off. It's crazy how it works but there is NO LIMITATION TO WHAT YOU CAN DO. I love nothing more in a game than that.
Please, buy this game.

This game only offers steam locomotives and its missions are positioned somewhere between 1850 to 1900.
The game spans across the territory of United States and the missions let you build the Trans Continental Railroad starting from New York and ending in San Francisco.
There are 10 missions and starting with the 4th, competitor AIs shows up on the map. The AI is not configurable and in some cases (and when you still didn't get the feel of the game) it can prove difficult. When fighting an AI your goal is to deliver more goods or transport more people to/from the city where you meet and compete. When someone wins the city, a monopoly sets in that lasts for 60 days.
I initially owned the CD version of this game that had some major problems (memory leaks) in the 8th mission especially when building Oil Rig stations.  The steam version has a similar problem (not as bad) in the 6th mission. I would just stay away from those Oil Rigs or just save before building a station there and if the lag appears just reload the game from that point.
When the game lags it almost becomes unplayable. The image just freezes and the days keep going in the background. You can end up losing 90% of your time just waiting for the game to unfreeze. But there is a workaround for this, you can just increase the bribe in the city hall and bribe everyone without having to work with your trains to send/receive goods. This only happened in the 6th mission for me, but Oil Rig stations may create additional problems.
Railroad Pioneer has the potential to be a great track laying and train management tycoon type game.
Unfortunately, it fails to deliver smooth gameplay mostly due to bugs/memory leaks. I would say that it is a good game and if you are patient with the bugs it's a must play for train tycoon fans. Definitely not a starter for those getting into this type of game. (The graphics are better than Railroad Tycoon 3 and my opinion is that the game aged pretty well, the multiplayer is also cool but has very few scenarios)

Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ what a journey.
I mean, the story is just so well done, the pacing is just superb. Just enough filler to keep you engaged so that when something important does come up, it feels all the more significant. The twists felt well built up to, and many of the characters felt like they had unique perspective, which is very difficult to pull off as well as Christine Love did. Really on a technical sense, there are generally very few bad things, and even those are just the smallest grammar nitpicks.
But the story itself is amazing. I wouldn't want to spoil anything, but I only want to say that it is
tragic. Romeo and Juliet (to pull the easiest metaphor) never knew such hopelessness, I swear. The two main characters give such a different perspective from each other concerning the events that I honestly think that it just would not have worked without either one of them.
The only issues I have are a minor bug concerning getting the 100% log completion and that it was a bit short; I passed the game in 2 sittings, 4 hours total (but I am a fast reader.) The rest of the time I spent trying to complete it without looking up walkthroughs, which did double my playtime.
All in all though, an amazing experience that will stay with me for a long time. Seriously get this (also the soundtrack. It's definitely worth it.)

A mythic tale of a frontier town, a farmstead, two brothers and a cursed sister, a priest, the devil and a horde of ferocious werewolves. Hell, that's a premise I wanted a piece of!
Alas, Sang-Froid is a good idea that lacks in execution in just about every way. The story is nicely thought out, but let down by crude visuals and all-around shoddy voice acting. The gameplay, which promises setting traps and fighting werewolves quickly shows it's true colours, revealing a simple yet quite unfair hack'n'slasher with fickle trap-setting underneath. The combat is hard, but for all the wrong reasons: your attacks do little damage unless boosted with some booze, your gun is next to useless against most enemies, the traps only affect some enemies and not all of them and while you wail away at an enemy that hides and regenerates health faster than you can kill it, another group of enemies has burned down a critical building on the other side of the map, causing you to have to restart the night!
I wanted to like Sang-Froid, but I just couldn't. It's a small-budget project trying to be a big-budget project, and the shortcomings bring it down like a house of cards.
Playtime: 4+ hours (ongoing)

Note that this review is based on just a few hours of play; I haven't completed the game yet.
Let me get this out of the way first: The cutscenes, both cinematic and in-engine, are pretty terrible and the story isn't anything to write home about.  The animation doesn't look especially good, the voice acting is sometimes questionable (on top of that, they don't pronounce things right for French Canadians which hurts my suspension of disbelief), and the writing occasionally veers into downright cringe-worthy.  I still appreciate that the cutscenes are there, since they do at least tie the missions/nights together, but I don't really enjoy them, per se.
Sang-Froid is sort of a combination 3rd-person action game and tower defense strategy, and fortunately, it pulls the gameplay off reasonably well.  The strategic and tactical elements of planning out your traps and then trying to execute your plan is quite satisfying.  The game has a surprising amount of little intricate details, like how your enemies can track you via sound and scent, and how you can use an intimidation system to buy yourself some breathing room, which come together with a variety of traps, many of which require some manual management on your part, to make a game that you can actually sometimes feel cunning during.  In a testament to the developers' enemy design, the monsters actually feel fairly varied, even though their variety is in reality little more than rock-paper-scissors, and they kind of fall to the same axework.
The game is at its strongest when you're planning your traps out, or rushing across the map to trip a net full of rocks just in the nick onf time.  You really get caught up in the moment, watching your plans come to fruition, or hearing the distant sound of a spike trap impaling a bunch of wolves while you're in the middle of a fight.
Unfortunately, the combat system doesn't measure up to the traps.  The ranged combat system has a far too aggressive auto-aim.  It's useful when you're trying to line up shots on circling wolves, as the rifle is meant to fire too slowly to make manual aiming feel rewarding.  But when you're trying to trigger one out of several clustered traps of nets filled with rocks, the game's inability to know which one you actually wanted to shoot as their autoaim fights each other can completely ruin a trap.  Not being able to move while reloading is frustraing, but I understand and accept the developer's decision in that regard, as it does make shooting the rifle "mean" more -- it makes using the weapon a resource beyond just the ammunition it takes, as the reload time can be a serious liability in the middle of a wave of enemies.
The melee combat system feels clunky and vague.  It's more like Don't Starve than Arkham Asylum or Assassin's Creed.  While hitting enemies with your axe is rewarding, the enemy "tells" for attacks are generally not obvious enough to make the dodge system really pay off.  You'll hit a werewolf twice, then suddenly get knocked over when they attack back, seemingly without warning.  You also have little control over what you're doing beyond "swing axe," so sometimes you'll knock enemies away when you'd rather be pressing the attack.  I find myself perpetually short of stamina, which probably means I'm fighting wrong, but it still is frustrating.   The real problem though is that while the enemies behave differently in terms of traps, in combat, they all seem to fight pretty much the same; or at least your tactics for fighting are pretty much the same.  All that changes is which weapon the enemy is particularly vulnerable to, which doesn't make for especially satisfying combat.  (Then again, I get the feeling that melee combat is *supposed* to be somewhat discouraged in the game, and almost making it dull does sort of discourage it.)
Each night is pretty short, but can be reasonably intense as the timing of some of your traps can be quite tight.  This gives each mission an almost bite-sized quality, so it's easy to play a couple nights in spite of a busy schedule.  It also lends itself to the "just one more" phenomenon in a way that longer missions would not.
Sang-Froid has its rough spots, but I feel that the game realizes the goals it set out to achieve, and by keeping itself short and sweet it manages to emphasize its fun parts and keeps the less fun parts from becoming tedious.

Analogue: A Hate Story is a visual novel unlike many others. You're presented with one objective: discover what happened to a certain ship, the Mugunghwa, through the logs of its dead crew. And of course, download said logs and get them to your employer. After all, you gotta get paid, ya' know?
But it goes deeper than that.
When I said it's unlike any others, I meant it. Unlike other VNs, you don't go to exotic locations, meet new characters, or stuff like that... all you got is a terminal. At least, at first. Because then, the cutest goddamn AI you could ever meet comes to greet you, gives you a display, and the game goes on.
And boy, does it go on.
It may seem short (Took me 6 hours to 100% the game), but I promise it will be worth your while. With an amazing. and for some people, minimalistic (even though I think it's prefectly fine that way) cast, a deep, rich storyline, moments that will make you laugh, moments that will make you cry, and moments that wil make you feel dread, and doubt your own morals and opinions you had at the start of the game... Analogue: A Hate Story is a must-have, in my opinion. It's easy to get into, REALLY easy to get hooked, and immensely satisfying to play through until the end.
And it has a sequel, Hate Plus, so you'll be able to get even more of the amazing duo that is *Hyung-ae and *Mute!
Overall, I give this game, a 9 out of 10. It was an amazing experience, and I would certainly buy it again if I could.

Although I had previously recommended this game on Steam, having recently finished my second full playthrough of
, I felt like I should accord it a proper review.
As an unabashed lore enthusiast, I must lead my review with praise for the world developer Christine Love created on board a generation ship lightyears into deep space. It is at once futuristic, yet historical; fantastical, yet grounded; beautiful, yet haunting. It is not the world which drew me to
, but it is certainly what drew me
it, making me want to read more and more about it, learn more about its society and people, and see it from the perspective of each and every of its inhabitants.
In many ways, it had to be what drew me in, as it will have to be what draws in anyone who plays it: unravelling the mystery of what happened on board the
is, after all, the sole meat of the game. Fortunately, Love's talent for writing made engaging with her world an easy task, bringing it to life with skill both technical and poetic. Though the game presents the player with numerous logs, letters, transcripts, and diary entries, each stands apart from the next through the care with which it was written. Each word seems carefully and deliberately chosen to present the reader with the most information in the most concise package, painting the narrative—and everything and everyone in it—with vibrancy and depth. Love knows players will spend a lot of time reading, and she takes care to waste none of it.
Too, Love's understanding of the human psyche shines in the way
's characters are brought to life. The AI constructs *Hyun-ae and *Mute, with whom the player interacts, reap the most visible benefits, and throughout the game I found myself caring for them, and empathizing with them, as though they were real. Yet even the characters we only read about in logs benefit here, each with their own unique personality and perspective. The style and tone with which each author writes reflects this, and aids the player in untangling
's dense narrative.
Aside from the writing, I will also take a moment to praise the game's other perks. Isaac Schankler's beautiful soundtrack can be both catchy and poignant, and I've listened to it outside of the game countless times.
's æsthetic is clean and refined in a way which puts to shame other visual novels, especially where the user interface is concerned. Finally, Love finds novel ways to utilize the Ren'Py engine's Python scripting system, and the game's sometime reliance on a command line interface certainly appealed to my inner nerd.
Although I have difficulty criticizing
, I would be negligent if I pretended the mechanics of play lived up to the game's otherwise high standard. The foremost issue I have is the series of binary dialogue options the player must use in response to the AIs *Hyun-ae and *Mute. This is explained as a technical limitation on the part of the protagonist's computer interface with said AIs and their ship, and while this fiction might excuse the crudeness of the mechanic better than other visual novels do, it's made frustrating by the way the player's responses are framed by the game. The story's morals, while delivered skillfully and subtly by the main narrative, were regrettably let down whenever I was made to choose one of two responses, when I properly agreed with neither.
Nevertheless, this one complaint should not sour you to the plethora of good things
has going for it.
is certainly my favorite video game of all time, and one I will recommend to anyone for whom it piques an interest.

The game itself at start felt overwhelming, kind of, but the tutorial was quite good. There are also a lot of helpers and tips that are given that can be turned off anytime you want it to be off.
The gameplay is very nice. It might be what you might expect out of a strategy base building game which honestly is pretty rare nowadays to pull off in a good fashion. It felt very addicting dieing all over again trying to survive the world itself. It was !!FUN!!
The user interface is actually pretty nice. It's easy to understand once you get the hang of it , It's not too cluttered up and simple, and it doesnt fill up your screen as you can see pretty much the entirety of what you want to see.
The difficulty setting is really good. How the game plays out caters to pretty much everyone, whether you just want to casually build on the rimworld to whether you want to brutally hurt yourself with unfair enemies and conditions. Not only that, there are 3 different "Difficulties AI" that can create a different pattern of difficulty. One that scales the threats upwards giving good amount of times and resources between every disasters, One that gives A LOT of times to build but a really strong army that bites hard whenever it comes by, and one that doesn't seem to have a set rule on when it want to give you threats or blessings; you just have to be ready.
The story it produces varies a lot. You will get attached to your colonists trying to help them survive each day, seeing them interact with each other, trying to survive the slaughters that are raids and the world trying to ♥♥♥♥ you itself with harsh conditions, surviving long winter with low amount of food supplies making that hard decision that maybe its time to kill your animals or maybe even friends to survive. And one day it will either end in a memorable fashion, or your colony will go through these phases and survive and go and become a big, rich colony that can defend itself.
The mod also helps if you really do want a different experience. Honestly probably everybody's view on rimworld is different due to this. A lot of people love vanilla, including me, but a lot of them loves dinosaurs and lovecraftian monsters in their game. The selection is great and can enhance the experience
The support for this game even though it is an early access game ,where they could have honestly abandoned it, is immense. It has gone through a lot of improvements with a humble developer(that recently got his team of members) that is active on forums.
The combat itself is quite RNGish but you still need to understand cover, how much a person can take, accuracy of your weapons and where you should take a fight, and whether or not you should
take cover or charge forward.
One of the bad things about the game is sadly, the enemy's AI. It has been improved times and times but they are too predictable at times. People found out ways to cheese the raids and enemies so badly already that it's possible to cheese through the midgames even the lategame. with tunnels and turrets, making the combat system obsolete.
Overall, an extremely solid and good game that somehow isnt getting the attention it deserves, 9.5/10

Utterly fantastic - in the truest sense of the word.
Take the insane setting of Borderlands (a world with equal parts humour and gore, and with some of the most well-written characters I've found), give it to the exceptional storytelling of Telltale Games (Sam & Max, Walking Dead, Wolf Among Us), add a sprinkle of drama and you get Tales of the Borderlands. Throughout the game, you play as both Rhys, a Hyperion worker looking to screw over his boss, and Fiona, a con artist after a score to end all scores. When things don't go quite to plan, the two unlikely partners (along with a motley group of accountants, robots and Vault Hunters) have to team up to find the Vault of the Traveller. It really doesn't help matters that the psycotic Handsome Jack isn't quite as dead as you'd like...
Gameplay wise, this isn't as deep as the classic adventuring of Sam & Max - there are very few "genuine" puzzles, and mostly the story is driven through your choices, much like TWD and WAU. A lot of the action is based around Quick Time Events, which are pretty forgiving but again feels like a bit of a cheap trick. I also get the feeling that, barring failed QTEs, it's pretty difficult to actually lose the game. The story must carry on, regardless of how awful you are.
That being said, the story is very, very well-written. Some of the choices are difficult ones to make, and the characters are so well acted that you start to fear for their safety. The humour had me laughing out loud frequently, and despite being QTEs, the action sequences were often spectacular.
All in all, definitely one for your library, ESPECIALLY when it's on offer.

This lightweight game is a typical F2P MMO, with the "Chinese MMO" style that was so popular in the late 00's/early 2010.
Based on The New Epoch Tabletop RPG (which sadly crashed in flames and ran out of... steam), City of Steam is less Steampunk and more Steam/Rune Fantasy. There's a more ethereal vibe to a majority of the quest hubs (which look radically different from the normal areas of the game).
The game reminds me a lot of Forsaken World and while I feel that game has a better art style (besides being a Steampunk myself), I think City of Steam is more worth playing due to it's accessibility and mechanic features.
Mechanist Games is based out of China, New Zealand and the United States, but the playstyle and art quality greatly resembles MMORPG's you saw in 2008 out of Korea/China.
City of Steam's worth playing if you're looking for a time killer or inspiriation in the Steampulp world.

I was really on the fence about whether to give this the thumbs up or down - after all, I did just spend something like €5 on it at the time. Is it worth €5? Well....maybe, but then I do have to consider that it was €35 on release, and there are any amount of excellent games you can get now for anything from €1 to €5, even in the FPS genre.
Pros:
- Great graphics at high/max settings, easily the best part of the game. Weapon models, environments (especially outdoor levels), enemies, etc all look great.
Cons:
- Horrible story with poor voice acting
- Pretty terrible AI behavior, reminiscent of early 2000's games
- Bad soundtrack that abruptly cuts out randomly depending on what's happening and then re-starts, pains the ears
- Feels sluggish to play even at 60fps compared to other shooters, movement is not good
- Very little scripting, it's just go from A to B shooting incredibly dumb enemies over and over
- Whole game just feels cheap in every conceivable way bar good graphics
It's very much trying to be like the original Call of Duty or Medal of Honor Allied Assault, and it is in some respects but the gameplay is just bad - despite the better graphics this is nowhere near as enjoyable as either game.
I would say despite my thumbs down it's worth a look at $3 if you're looking for some brainless shooting with brilliant graphics, but don't expect good or even passable gameplay. After one hour playing it, I felt like it was a major chore.

This is a good remaster, but the devs pushed it out the door and just left it alone. There hasn't been a single update. What gives? Anyway, let's get to what's new here.
Dead Island itself is a great game. It's a good zombie game and Techland's first jab at the zombie genre before making the fantastic Dying Light. A few years later, here we are with a remaster of the game. Is it good? Well, it's mixed, but it's still good to me nonetheless, maybe because I got it for $3. Anyways, let's talk about the good things first.
The new graphics are great. I love them. There's new textures that are sharper and crisper than the original. There's also a brand new engine from what I've heard, as the remaster was also a port to the new Chroma Engine 6, the same engine as Dying Light (parkour not included), which also introduces some great new lighting. It's a joy to look at.
But the new paint comes with a cost. The game is a resource hog. Whereas the old game runs with no problems, this game gets frame drops. Granted it isn't impossible to run, and I can pull off 60 FPS on my EVGA GTX 960 4GB without turning everything down to medium or low, but it's still a nuisence nonetheless. The main menu was strangely locked to 30 FPS, where the last game wasn't. Why? It just seems like a stupid design decision that was not needed at all. There also seems to be missing DLC from what I've read in the reviews. I haven't bought the DLC for Dead Island before or have played it in years since my Xbox 360 days, so I don't know what it is, but I feel like I should bring it up.
This remaster of Dead Island is good. It could be better, but what we got is still good. I just dislike how the devs still haven't released any patches fixing bugs or improving optimization. Why? Why leave this game behind so quickly?
Should you buy?

Prototype 2 is basically just more of the same. Some game mechanics have been slightly tweaked, but overall it's the same game with a different character.
The story is paper thin and aside from the occasional insight into Blackwatch and the science teams fighting the infection, the story might as well not be there at all. Heller, like Mercer in the original game, has absolutely no regard for human life and basically turns into a killing machine the moment the game starts. Except for one situation in the game where he suddenly shows compassion for one single person. His one-liners are enjoyable but as a protagonist he does very little else to wow you.
The virus, mutations, upgrades, weapons and shape shifting are the bread and butter of this game. 99% of the time you will be hacking, slashing and impaling Blackwatch soldiers and infected alike with your shape shifting blades and other goodies. As you progress through the game these weapons will become more and more powerful. If you take the time to do side missions this gets to a point where Heller becomes completely overpowered and is able to easily kill anything that gets in his way. Some upgrades even make you immune to small arms fire, making it possible to ignore the majority of the military all together while avoiding rockets.
While this kind of power is very fun to play around with, it takes away just about any challenge the game had left to offer. Any enemy that can't be killed in 3 hits can easily be avoided and with a huge surplus of consumeable people around you will never (ever) run out of health. While I played the game on Normal, I can't imagine the game being any more challenging on Hard.
It's still a very fun game to play around in. But if you are looking for a solid story or a game that offers a challenge then you best keep searching. This is basically a hack and slash version of GTA and nothing more. Recommended to get when it's on sale.

I like Sang-Froid - Tales of Werewolves for 3 reasons:
1) The game play - It has a great mix between 3rd person action (smashing wolfs with axes, guns and what not); stragety in terms of placement of fire, traps and where you put your charcter & upgrading of your weapons and traps between the action.
2) I love the setting - and the idea of a remote french canadian forrest town harrased by warewolves.
3) Different monsters require different tactics making you try different ways to bring them down
What i didnt like about it:
a) I found the story is a bit weak and i ended up skipping the cutsceans towards the end - i just didnt buy into the emotion behind saving your sick sister - the voice acting was fine, but it could perhaps have better script writing.
b) Ended too quickly - just when i was getting into the gameplay it was all over.
c) Little replayability - some variety is very much needed to make me want to play it again, such as a much harder difficulty level so i can test my skills - also some randomisation in where the monsters spawn as once you have fuigured out the tactic to a map - there is little incentivve to try another tactic.
Would i recomend it? YES! and i very much hope the developers will relsease an expansion / DLC with more maps, more characters, more weapons as the gameplay is very fun and is the true highlight og the game.

Borderlands is a FPS RPG with Diablo-esque twist to it. Though it may not have been the very first to start the genre, it definitely gave the genre the boost into mainstream spotlight that really put it into the light.
I've held off writing a review until I completed the game, which I had no incentive to since I wanted to play this game with my friends when it initially came out and just recently got to playing with them again. Gameplay wise, it's to be expected that it's much less detailed and fun than Borderlands 2, but it's to be expected as the streamliner for the series.
You play as one of 4 different characters with different ability sets and unique abilities, pushing for your character to play in a certain style but not forcing it onto you. It's an FPS, but you also get scrolling combat dmg and experience to level as well as a loot grade system much like Diablo. As to be expected of one of the very first in the genre and as a game from 2009, it's got much to polish up on, but if you like to see the roots of the genre and still have fun, I'd definitely try it.
Pros:
+ Lots of guns and different uses for them, electric guns are much more effective against shields, corrosive is effective against armor, etc.
+ Get to shoot disabled midgets and crazy giants in the face with rocket launchers
+ FPS RPG
Cons:
- Quest doesn't allow you to see multiple objectives at a time, forcing you to backtrack in some cases
- Unclear with Fast Travel locations
- Eventually becomes very tedious
- Needs polishing up on a lot of things in the game
- Clap-Trap
TL;DR:
Borderlands is a FPS RPG with Diablo-esque twist to it. One of the first in the genre, has a dire need of polishing up which Borderlands 2 takes care of, but it's still a great game.

Loved it the moment it came out in 2009 and I'm still running around in Pandora (including Borderlands 2 & The Pre-Sequel) today! I couldn't recommend the series anymore or rate it any higher.
OK ... so I'm a Borderlands franchise fanboy, but don't think that this recommendation comes with lots of doses of bias, I have introduced a couple of my friends to the Borderlands series and they have become Borderlands nuts also. But, what's not to like, it is the perfect drop in /drop out fast paced shooter, it has tons of missions to do (even more when you add the DLC's), it is pure Gun Porn with the amount of weapons that you can find, it's gameplay is as addictive as hell, it is very funny (Claptrap is a LEGEND in my eyes lol), the sheer amount of challenges/achievements, tons of lootable objects, that rainbow shower of goodies when you pop off the tougher enemies, and the cartoon style craphics just finish it off perfectly ... now add 4 player co-op for ultimate buddy fun!!!
Now the CONS, only two really.
Well, one, sort of, and one wish.
1/ (Con)
The fact that you cannoy move once in Second Wind when playing single player, both Borderlands 2 & The Pre-Sequel allow movement in Second Wind. Nothing worse than being put into Second Wind and end up stuck behind some scenery or cover and unable to target an enemy to get that Second Wind kill because you can't move. F-R-U-S-T-R-A-T-I-N-G!!!
1/(Wish)
That Borderlands + it's DLC's, just as they are (don't forget to include the Scythid as an enemy stat to kill this time), be re-made/transferred into the Borderlands 2 Engine. And while I'm wishing, now that all three games use a Badass Ranking system, why not make your Badass Ranking carry over into the next game ie, Borderlands -> Borderlands 2 -> The Pre-Sequel, now that would be cool.
