The folk music in this is really great, it's moody and well utilized to draw you in right from the start.  The music is certainly the best part of the game.  I'll give a nod to the interesting art design as well, but the execution is pretty sub-par.
The game itself is a mashup of tower defense and third person brawler/shooter, with the map you're defending expanding after each round as you unlock new tools and resources.  There's promise there, but it's poorly delivered on and ultimately provides a choppy and inconsistant experience.
The plot is... bad.  It's bad.  It's reall, really, so very bad.  It seems promising at the start, but by the second or third round it's almost bad enough to be ironically entertaining.  The devil is particularly amusing, while the depiction of the natives actually verges on upsetting.
There are better games out there that deliver on this mechanical concept more fluidly, and there are better stories about werewolves in frontier times.  But it's too bad the sound track isn't available as a seperate purchase.

It's well known that the developers of Interstellar Marines are currently looking to find a publisher to help them with continued development of the game. My heart really goes out to the dev team as they're obviously committed to the game and the vision they have for it. It's very sad that every setback one could think of for a dev team has in fact happened to the IM dev team. More so that the game only appears to have a small number of dedicated fans.
Let me be clear: this game deserves to do incredibly well. Why? Well, it's not yet another COD clone and very much has its own style and atmosphere, not to mention quite a cool setting that will hopefully allow for endless and varied content going forwards.
Though these features of the game would be more than enough for me to support it, the real reason I love Interstellar Marines is that the core game mechanics are so well done and feel so solid. From sound effects to the toggleable helmet HUD to the ambient environment effects (that can and do change) in missions, the way your character moves, to the sound & handling of the weapons - this game just *feels* like I'm a special forces operator involved in secret sci-fi tactical operations. Everything has an authentic, sci-fi but real feel to it.
Content as it is now is somewhat sparse. That being said, there are a few single player missions and a good number of MP maps to keep players going. This is another aspect of the game that I really love - the game has a laser-like focus on tactical squad action. An analogy: I felt that the recent Doom re-boot gave what is probably the purest 'traditional' FPS experience since the original Unreal Tournament. What Doom has done for the 'traditional' FPS, Interstellar Marines does for the tactical shooter. Little fuss and nonsense but a finely hones focus on core gameplay. It all just works. The core game play works incredibly well and feels fun and exciting to play.
I really, really hope that the dev team manage to find a publisher who will support them and enable them to get IM finished and development back up to speed. As it is the game is genuinely fun to play and as I've noted all of the core game mechanics are tight and work incredibly well. With the right support IM could be, and deserves to be, huge.

I am a big fan of the game Dwarf Fortress, and lost many of my evenings having "fun" while trying to build a thriving dwarf city.  Seldom does a game come around like that, and introduce an entirely new form of computer game entertainment.
This is not Dwarf Fortress.  It is pretty close, though.
And, in not being Dwarf Fortress, it takes the opportunity to do many things a whole lot better than it's predecessor.
So far, I've only played the game "vanilla."  In that state, it is a tremendously enjoyable game.  You start with 3 colonists, and you go from there.  I've grown one colony to 16 people, which may be the limit of my patience.  I had the opportunity for more, but began turning colonists away.
I've also have the opportunity to lose miserably a handful of times.  And each time, I found myself laughing at the spectacle of stupidity I'd been conned into attempting (leading to my own demise).
Overrun by angry Muffalo.  Check.
Overrun by angry Antelope.  Check.
Entire colony fried when attempting to fight an out of control fire in a stone building.  Check.
Starved to death.  Check.
Other methods of "fun" have been discovered as well, but these are the ones that made me chuckle.
I almost skipped this game after reading some of the reviews.  I feared that this was a shallow knock-off on DF and similar titles, and I was given the impression there are some gaping misses in worker AI.  I'd read several discussions about fires being out of control (and constant).  And, I'm thrilled that I didn't let that scare me away.
So far, I've found a very stable, reasonably well balanced game.  One that is highly enjoyable, has good replay, and lets me exercise my planning ahead skills some.
If you're a DF veteran, here's what you might consider to be "cons".  This would be vanilla; there are probably mods to address some of these:
- Single-level building.  The playing area is 2-D
- Limited number of items to decorate with.  As you unlock technologies, you gain stuff, but overall, the ornamentation is minimal.
- Building of many items, like beds, tables, etc., is done "in place," making it difficult to just turn out 10 tables at a workbench and keeping the best.
That's probably the worst of it.  So much is done remarkably well, though, it entirely makes up for these issues.
I highly recommend this game.  I hope you enjoy it!

What can I say? I'm a huge fan of the Naruto series. It's one of those rare animes that really reach deep into your core. This game is a beautiful tribute to the Naruto anime that takes you back to the reconstruction of the Leaf after the fight with Pain up to the fight with Tobi and the Tailed Beasts.
What I love about this game:
+ Beautiful graphics
+ Very satisfying fighting mechanics
+ Sticks to the Naruto story well and accurately
+ Online/multiplayer batteling
+ So many characters to choose to fight as
+ You don't just fight as Naruto, you fight as other characters as well
+ Cutscenes: there are a lot, and sometimes are long. If you can't stand long cutscenes you have the option to skip them (I did not)
+ Some fights challenged you
Cons (for some people but not for me in some cases):
- Some of the fights got waaayy too tough (which is fine) and they give you the option to heal but it lowers the rank you recieve. Some fights you just have to heal or you won't win. However, you won't get higher than a D.
- Does sometimes get intense on my computer. If you can't stand fps drops make sure your specs are good enough to play (they didn't bug me too much but at times it was annoying)
- 30 fps lock (again, not an issue for me)
This game is a tad pricey but it's worth it. The main story will take aomewhere around ~18 hours. If you are a huge Naruto fan like I am, this game is a must have.

I'll be frank.
This game was enjoyable and I think it's a good timewaster. However, please note that I paid $3.40 for it. I mention the price because it's a big reason why this game gets a 'yes' recommendation from me.
Don't get me wrong. Like I said, I enjoyed it and it can be fun, especially due to the political/cultural aspect, which is something I personally like. However, the story simply isn't that strong.
To begin, the story is paper thin and mostly centers around 'the Pale Bride' -- a name which suggests more mystery and intrigue than the game eventually reveals. The plot is focused on what happens with this Pale Bride and what happens to the inhabitants of the ship. There are actually quite a few other mysteries, but the game never even tries to resolve them, so those two are the ones that receives focus. Meanwhile, the story that the game does focus on tends to be nonsensical most of the times and mundane at other times.
This is alright as this is an indie game and short one at that. I don't expect the developers to perform magic by creating a mind-blowing story in such circumstances. However, due to lack of content, shortness, and a weak story, I wouldn't recommend paying more than $5 for the game. Wait for a deal to pop up if you're interested.

"Visual novel" is a term that usually means "campy dating sim." I mean, there's nothing WRONG with a campy dating sim, coming from a guy who's played a few, but VNs rarely have the complexity one looks for in a novel.
is...different. Once you brush past the moe anime trappings of the two AIs, you find a science fiction novel that would be right at home on a bookshelf with the works of Ursula K. LeGuin, Margaret Atwood, or a pre-awful-human-being Orson Scott Card.
is, essentially, a virtual epistolary novel--a phrase which here means "a book made of documents from random dudes/dudettes." Much like the now-lauded
, it's up to the reader to piece together what happened to wipe out an entire ship of potential planetary colonists. Here's a hint, folks: AWFUL THINGS.
Both AIs--*Hyun-Ae and *Mute-- are engaging characters, but it's *Hyun-Ae who steals the show in this installment. (*Mute gets her own time to shine in the follow-up,
.) *Hyun-Ae is likable, mysterious, and somehow unnerving all at once. As the player learns more about her, they begin to realize that there's quite a bit *Hyun-Ae is hiding...and *Mute might have good reason not to trust her.
is, by the end of the story, one of the darkest games I've played. Even the joke ending can't erase the horrors that led an entire ship full of human beings to its death. Like a lot of great sci-fi (especially from the silver age and onward),
uses the far future to talk about our present, and what lies immediately ahead. While it does (depending on your actions) end on a redemptive note, the story haunts you. I still think about
from time to time, and I can't say that for many games--indie or triple A. For that reason, I recommend this game wholeheartedly.

Five problematics out of five.
Deus Vult!
In all seriousness, this is a surprisingly polished game. There isn't a lot to it, structure-wise: you have three levels and four skill trees, and you use a machine gun, rocket launcher, and five different support abilities to destroy waves of attacking soldiers and vehicles. It's very reminiscent of classic arcade games, both in its structure and in its difficulty.
Its simplicity works in its favor, given how the game progresses. You aren't just completing a stage by defeating X waves of enemies and moving on to the next; your objective is to last as long as possible against an increasingly intense assault, with your eventual score ranked according to both your number of kills and the length of time you spent alive. At the beginning of the game, you're going to die early and often, but as you play, you rack up skill points which you can invest into persistent upgrades across attempts.
As you unlock increasingly powerful abilities, you find yourself able to last just a little bit longer each time, and there's a real element of challenge involved in learning how and when to use your support abilities as well as what to prioritize and when. The real challenge of the game is not to finish all three maps (which will happen pretty much no matter what, as "finishing" a map is as simple as racking up a certain number of kills across your playthroughs), but to push yourself to see how long you can last. And you will eventually lose: like the recently released Devil Daggers, "winning" just means getting further than anyone else before you bite it.
My main criticism is a lack of enemy variety: there are normal old soldiers, suicide bombers, technicals, humvees, and three types of landing craft (pontoons, and small and large troop carriers). I'd have liked to see more, different types of soldiers (engineers, grenadiers, machinegunners) or enemy air units. But for the price, and the amount of visual spectacle going on, this is an easy recommendation for a few hours of relaxing rat-a-tat.

UnReal World is an old-school, RPG turn-based survival game. It's not overly hard, but the complexity and learning process will likely lead to a few untimely deaths.
Every single movement causes a slight passage in time. Take a step forward, time passes. Turn left or right, time passes. Activities, such as pulling brush off a tree, skinning an animal, filling a cup with water, or crafting some gloves brings up a progress bar while time passes automatically (with the option to stop mid-activity.) Doing something time consuming, such as building a wall for your shelter, generally takes some planning as you have to pay attention to your hunger/thirst/temperature/energy while doing so. Seems pretty standard, but when you're tracking some big game and the tracks converge on a heavily traffic area, turning left or right to look around means that animal gets further away.
The controls are somewhat confusing as there are key bindings for every activity. There's in-game help, but it might be more helpful to find a wiki that will list all actions in an easy to access format. Of course, as with all games, you should hopefully get used to it eventually.
The game is available for free outside of Steam, so if you're on the fence, I highly recommend grabbing it and giving it a shot. However, if you like it, PLEASE buy it because something like this deserves support. This game has been in development for 20~ years and they keep going.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

...Where to begin on this one...
Well,I've always enjoyed physics platformers and puzzle games,so when I
saw a physics driving game for $1 I thought "Hey,why not?"
...Oh...
Lets go over it piece by piece
To start,the graphics are almost non-existent,just base texture,nothing
special or attractive whatsoever.But there's more to a game than just
graphics,so it dosen't bother me. What DOES bother me however is some
textures will just dissapear at times,they'll still be there to drive
on,just invisible...a um...slight problem.
The sound is also mostly absent,there's no music,and the only sounds are
a standard engine noise and a thump if you impact
something...however,sometimes when you respawn the vehicle, the sound
will simply cut off entirely and not return.
The playable vehicles? just one wireframe dune-buggy looking
thing...that's it.
But the real issues come in the gameplay,it's a standard driving
game,the "Physics" comes in the form of obstacles,speed-bumps,breakable
barriers,loops etc...and in most areas the track has no walls,meaning
you can fall off to your doom almost anywhere,with checkpoints few and
far between.
Now anyone who's ever played a game with a racetrack creator has
probably at some point decided to make "THA MOZT IMPOZZIBULL TRAKC
EVARRRRRR!!! :D" and proceeded to do so,only to realize that it wasn't
any fun to slowly inch around a track avoiding hazards.Welp,there are
hazards OVER THE ENTIRE TRACK! Most enjoy driving games for the sense of
speed,but you have to plod through this too slowly to get any
enjoyment...one tiny mistake and it's back to the last checkpoint...but
hey,maybe you like obstacle courses?...you won't on this,as most
obstacles are designed to infuriate you instead of providing fun or a
challenge,thin rails to drive across,speedbump clusters that go on
forever...obstacles that come up THROUGH the track as you drive over
them...it's all pretty bad....
...So...how are the  "Physics"?
Well,sometimes taking a speedbump slowly will send you flying into
orbit,sometimes you'll lose all traction and slide off the
road,sometimes you'll just fall THROUGH the road,and it seems if so much
as one wheel isn't touching something solid,the other three wheels lose
all traction...soo...yeah, this is a BIG PROBLEM! Especially on a course
that requires precision.There's also the speed issue,as I said,you have
to inch through this,but some areas require great speed,loops for
example,however some don't have enough space in front of them to
properly build up speed,others you can get the speed just fine,only to
find a near unavoidable obstacle immediatly on the other side...given
the track design, momentum is a constant issue,as you always either have
too much or not enough. Also,when your vehicle falls off the track or
wrecks you press R to respawn,but this sometimes glitches,for
example:keeping your fall momentum and having you just bounce off the
track at the respawn point,or respawning INSIDE of something. I'm sure
there's more problems I've forgotten to mention,but you get the point.
But through it all I persisted,to claim those sweet achievements and
defeat this beast!!! However,the steam achievements...didn't work...I
did what they say to do to unlock them,but nothing...NOT ONE worked.But
whatever,did I beat the game? Well i got to the end...only to have one
last obstacle,a block that appeared from beneath the track,pop up as I
drove over it and flip me off the road...still determined I made my way
back to find...the block was still there,blocking the exit...with no way
around it...I tried respawning several times,but nothing would make it
dissapear,so I was either glitched,or it was designed to where you had
one shot to clear it. And while you have checkpoints,there is no save
feature in this,so if I closed the game,i would have to start over from
the beginning...I'M DONE!
I  can only hope this was either someones first ever attempt at making a
game,or a clever satire of how easy it is to get bad games published on
Steam,but regardless this was HORRIBLE. Not a fun type of bad you can
enjoy ironically,just pure BAD.
So in conclusion...
DON'T DO THIS TO YOURSELF!!!

The greatest flaw with this game is the design of the gameworld. The very first area I was thrown into was wide and open...and completely barren. And I'm not just talking in terms of the appearance of the area, but of the design. Yes, there was a huge area for me to go around in, but that space was filled with nothing. Repeated textures for trees and dry bushes, random enemies with no rhyme or reason to their design were rampant, and I was left with the feeling I was walking around a huge chessboard, not the desert area I was supposedly wandering in.
Heading to what I could only presume was the hub city, I was greeted with more of the same. The city was a wide open space, but still empty. What fills the world are either a combination of random swarms of enemies you combat with a subpar, unrealized magic system, and NPCs with mismatched voicework and little to no reason to care for them. This on top of the needlessly cluttered, unorganized spellbook make the game a chore, and all for little to no reward.
Maybe the game gets better later. Maybe those first few areas are the black sheep and the world becomes alive and interesting later, and somehow the magic system starts functioning without being needlessly obtuse. But if just playing the tutorial and two starting areas make me as unexcited and eye-rollingly critical as this game's starting areas made me, I doubt the rest of it is worth it.

To put my praise into one sentence: It's like this game is part 3 in a series. That is to say, it has so many interesting mechanics and ideas at work, you'd swear they were introduced over several games. But no -- somehow, Artifice has managed to come up with a half dozen new ideas all at once, and each builds on the last wonderfully.
By far the most important is the "fear factor" -- this system really makes it feel like you're fighting a pack of wolves, unlike every other game where enemies just run up to you without thought. I never knew I wanted a "realistic" wolf fighting game before, but there you are.
Aside from the gameplay, the music is impressive and catchy, but most other aspects do fall a little short. The graphics are dated and the voice actors aren't remotely up to the job. But the game itself is so different and fun that I can easily look past those flaws.
My only other complaint is that with every stage introducting new things, there isn't much time to play around with each individual feature. It sounds odd to basically want filler, but having a second stage between each change would make it feel less rushed. On the other hand, it does contribute to an on-edge atmosphere, since you have to deal with the unknown every single level.

Fate is a Cruel Mistress.
I'm a pretty big fan of RPG's, and generally enjoy RPGmaker games.  However, this game has some issues.  The big problems are that the storyline is convoluted and uninteresting while the characters are boring and you never get attached to any of them.  But, you can appreciate what the developer was trying to do so those aspects tend to be "not good enough" rather than "painful."
The smaller issues are what really kill this game.  Grammatical mistakes, terrible dialogue, game bugs / flaws, achievements that don't work, unclear path to progression, etc.  There is even confusion on movement speed as you start the game with the ability to run around at rapid speeds, but inexplicably lose that ability after an hour or so and never get it back (which is super bad later on since you do a lot of wandering around).  Especially given the price point on this game, I really cannot recommend it.  If you do find it on a good sale, I would still say that only the most zealous RPGmaker fans should apply.  Give this game the fate that it deserves, the fate of the forgotten.

Estranged Act 1 is surprisingly good considering it is a comunity built game with no commercial backing, done for fun.
If you are expecting a Tripple-A grade game, you probably should look elsewhere, but keep in mind this is completely free.
The atmosphere is quite good, as are many of the elements of the level layout.  The world does feel tangable and coherant, and has a lot of small details that make it more immerisve.   Little drawings and readable notes and whiteboards all make things more interesting, and make it feel like you are going through a real workplace where something went horibly wrong.   It definately leaves me wanting to know more.
As of the problems:
The biggest issue has to be the NPC animations.  Many of them are simply non-existant.   The zombies more stumble around, rather than stagger, and there is very little in the way of animation.
In some spots the difficulty feels artificially added through making the machine gun weaker, and artificially improving the abilities of the AI to land good hits.  This is particularly so when you are assaulted in the warehouse.  Generally the AI on these tactical units is quite good.
The layout of many of the levels isn't the best.  There is an excessively liniar feel to them.
The zombie placement is a little predictable and their spawning sometimes comes from nowhere.  However, that is a very common problem in many games.
As of the graphics, they aren't too bad, but they aren't particularly good either.   There are definately plenty of places they could be improved, such as the detail plants, and a few textures.  However, in other spots they look better than some comercial games on the same engine.   I have to say the rocky cliff side in one spot is downright exceptional.  The real disappointment is the lack of consistancy

A more or less epic quest to find peace and salvation brings the hero of this game in a very awkward situation...
The graphics are simply the RPGMaker stuff that is available.
Standard RPGMaker sound too...
Just your average JRPG created by RPGMaker...
Important Values for Genre:
The story comes like a bit of a surprise, the game has it's offs, but once you get started with the game, you actually will try to finish it. The main protagonist of the game is "Gauly" a unlikely hero (more an typical antihero) who is hunted, abused and... well you'll see when you play the game. Though the game doesn't look like much, it's a lot of gametime involved - the story will develop during the game and will take twists and turns. Some things have to be taken with care, though, there are some inconsistencies around.
Standardized RPGMaker Routines, nothing special, nothing out of the ordinary.
The game has surprised me, once I started it, I couldn't put it aside. Yes I know, it's a cheap RPGMaker game. But well, try it yourself, and play it through... the story has it's flaws as I stated. Positive is, that the game actually draws you into it's plot.
The game isn't too bad, but it isn't special too. The story works fine for this game, so it might be worth a try. Spellchecking would also be a nice addition, before it got released.
The game has some more hours of playtime! But that isn't sufficient enough because most of it is grinding experience Levels with the most officious monsters possible at given level. The Balancing though is ok, and the game had no crashes, or gamebreaking bugs during play.
The game is a bit expensive to give it a full recommendation, plus it's quite standard RPG-Maker stuff. If you get it on a cheap sale, or somewhere else give it a try...
If you are not a fan of RPG (especially JRPG's) or long grinding hours, don't buy this game.

Tower-defense/action hybrids have appeared to become a genre on their own.  Games like Orcs Must Die and Sanctum seem to lead the pack in this realm but Sang-Froid has emerged to be my favorite of this style of game.  First off, I love the aesthetic of the game.  The frozen Canadian frontier in December during the 1800s really appealed to me.  Couple this with the werewolf and Native American lore and I was hooked.  There is story here.  The voice acting and animation definitely show it's indie roots (meaning not that great) but unlike other games of this ilk, I actually paid attention to the narrative.
Gameplay wise, strategy is key.  Know where to place your traps and what kind of traps to use is crucial.  The planning phase of this game ended up being more instrumental to me than any other tower defense game.  It was extremely satisfying during missions to here a trap go off somewhere in the distance and know I had a kill.  The combat might be the weakest part of this game.  You could say it was "challenging" but at times it just seemed clumsy.  I would often swing my ax at an enemy and get caught in a combat animation that would leave me vulnerable.  I don't know if this was intentional but it felt frustrating at times.  However, when it worked, I enjoyed it.
Overall:
Pros:  Decent story, good atmosphere, great strategy, interesting enemies.
Cons:  Clumsy combat, somewhat stiff voice acting.
I would reccommend this game.  Extra reccommendation: play it in the winter when there is snow on the ground outside  if you can.  This definetly added to my enjoyment of the game.
UPDATE: Now it is free so you have no excuse not to try it.

-Sigh- This game... Where do I start? Okay. Before you say anything about my playtime, listen. My friend told me that Soccer Manager 2016 came out not too long ago. 2015 was okay even though it had problems, but I was like "hm, let's see what they did with the game". So me and him checked out the game for like an hour. Now, I downloaded the game just so I could write this review. And this is basically what I got from that hour of playtime.
First thing that bothered me is the whole "share with friends" thing. Okay. I get it. You want that friends compare the state of their clubs and stuff, BUT STOP TELLING ME TO SHARE EVERYTHING WITH MY FRIENDS THE WHOLE TIME! Jesus, you start the game, why don't you SHARE IT WITH YOUR FRIENDS?! Sign a player, SHARE IT WITH YOUR FRIENDS! Could you PLEASE stop shoving those words in my face, I already said NO! I don't have to share it with my friends, mostly because most of my friends would never play this.
Secondly, why did you remove the feature where we could make our own formation? Makes no sense. I want to have some freedom when deciding the team tactics... I'm supposed to be the MANAGER, the creative mind of the club, yet I'm being limited to default formations? Also, the player info doesn't appear as a pop-up... Why? It was fine as it was. It's a small thing, yeah, but it was good as it was.
Third point, your team (i.e. West Ham) may win 3-0 against City, but then they will lose against Shrewsbury in the FA Cup 4-0, even when you use the same team that beat City. "Realistic" simulation, huh?
I could ignore all of that... But I can't ignore this: THE GODDAMN SHOP.
Now, I understand. It's a Free-To-Play game but you still want to make money for the hours of time spent on developing the game. But come on... You LITERALLY can't do ANYTHING without buying stuff from the shop! In FM, you can ask the board for more money. Here, there is no football board, and in order to get money, you have to pay REAL MONEY?!
If you want to make money, why not just charge for the game, and not have this BS of a shop system.
Although these points have only been negatives, I like the game, I want to support it because I think it has potential. But the thing is, the potential is fading away. You can't say it's realistic when I can add 80 million in cash to my team's bank with real money. When the club needs money, it's the BOARD that gives it. Not the MANAGER. You can't market the game as realistic when these kind of stuff are in the game. I get so annoyed when a game has so much potential, but then they blow it.
I think it's a 5/10 game. You can try the game out yourself if you want to. It's not bad, but the points I mentioned above make it fall to the below-average category.
As for me, I'll stick with FM.

Tales from the Borderlands has humour, tension, sadness. The entire plethora of emotions.
You play 90% of the game past-tense. The 2 main characters, Rhys and Fiona, are on a long walk with someone who has captured them and they tell that person what

Telltale always have
at the start of each episode where you play 10 minutes then a 1-2 minute long clip is played introducing you to Episode X.
This game, out of all the Telltale games, had the best episode intros.
The fact that 90% of the game is played past-tense took away from the excitement of the game-play as I know that no matter what happens in my game-play, the 2 main characters survive without damage, for the most part.

IS Defense is a first person shooting gallery in which the player defends various European areas against an endless supply of fanatical and militant Mohammedans.
Occurring in the year 2020, it depicts an expanded and aggressive ISIS assuming control of the entire Middle East (including apparently Israel) and North Africa, after which it sets its sights across the Mediterranean Sea.  Not content with mere infiltration of Middle Eastern refugee groups, these undocumented immigrants invade Europe equipped with everything from their conventional armaments (small arms, technicals, skiffs) to military grade weaponry (humvees, armored troop transport ships, etc.).
The game is very similar to Beach Head 2000 and its sequels, but avoids many of Beach Head's shortcomings by including more contemporary game mechanics such as skill points (which unlock features like faster reload times, explosive ammunition, and increased health), the ability to summon power-ups (supply drops, allied infantry, and apparently airstrikes and mortar bombardments (the last two I haven't yet experienced in the game, though certain parts of the skill tree that I haven't yet unlocked indicate such elements)), and having more than one environment (the game starts the player defending the shores of Sicily, with other settings becoming accessible only after a certain number of enemy troops and vehicles are eliminated; the progress carries over into each new game), so IS Defense, while still easily accessible to the less than hardcore gamers, is also a lot more advanced than the more casual Beach Head games.
An extra touch I particularly enjoy about the game is the roaming camera that sweeps the area after death.  The oncoming hordes are still rushing and chanting their war cries, carcasses litter the scene (there's a feature under the advanced graphics options to have the corpse limit set to "unlimited"), any remaining allied troops still fight to the last man, and I've even seen enemy vehicles fatally run over their own jihadists!  Any supply drops requested just before death are also shown faithfully carrying out their last mission, so I wouldn't be surprised if I see enemy fighters get crushed by the dropped crates someday.
Overall, this is an excellent effort from a gaming studio of modest means, and I hope to see some DLC for it in which the player must defend American shores from the Islamofascists.

Overall, this game has potential if actual effort is put into it. As of right now it's just too similar to an asset flip with a price that will make you go "Welp, sounds interesting and it's only a dollar!" . Don't bother unless it's patched or updated in the future. And no, this is not early access. Yikes.

As a fan of RPG maker games, I've played my fair share.
I've played some excellent titles such as Sydney's World, and Vagrant Hearts 1 & 2.
They had interesting stories, unique and memorable characters, excellent battle systems, and very good interfaces.
This game doesn't make me feel the same way.
It should be noted that the Vagrant Hearts series came out from this same developer after Fated Souls.
Fated Souls is a very generic turn-based RPG.
It features a side view battle system, a handful of different characters, and random battles.
Typical problems with the RPG Maker engine are here such as no Steam Overlay support.
I'm surprised to see that this game costs full price $10.99 CDN. This game is NOT worth that much by any means. There is simply not enough good qualities here to make this game worth that price.
I've also discovered that some Steam Achievements do NOT work in this game for those who care.
Pros:
-Good battle system
-Player characters are animated (I don't see this in RPG Maker games very often)
-Decent music and sound effects
There is simply not enough here to make me want to keep spending my time playing. Everything about this game is just so generic, and there are too many spelling and grammarical errors to take the attempt at good writing here seriously. I found the story very unusual, and the characters were very strange. The main character was a very moody childish person. I found it unappealing.
Travelling from town to town through maze-like forests got very boring eventually, especially once I realized that this was the main path of progression in this game. It just felt so boring and generic.
The interface is very bland. The artwork is terrible. The portraits of the characters don't match the in game sprites and one of the characters portrait is zoomed in way more that the rest of them and it just looks bad.
For some reason, your main character walks around at lighting speed during the first hour or so of the game. No, there is no Walk/Run button or game setting. The walking speed than changes later in the game automatically to something more tolerable.
I found this made no sense and was a very memorable negative about the game design.
No attempt was made here to make this game stand out as exciting or impressive.
I think the issue here is that this is the first game this developer made, and Vagrant Hearts is proof he got better at this, but this game has no buisness being priced the way it is.
I guess I just expect a lot more out of a game released within the last couple years, since everyone else is doing much better things with the engine.
There is no excuse for the bad spelling and grammer, and broken achievements. It's 2016, let's act like it.
MAYBE, get this game if you have nothing else better to play, and you can get it for a low price, otherwise don't waste your time.There are plenty of better RPGs on Steam with lower or equal prices tags than this.
Skip this game, you're not missing anything.

In Fated Souls the main character (Gauly) is thrown into an innocent enough sounding situation wherein he is called on to escort a maiden (and her mentor) of the "Great Church" to a faraway temple. Simple enough, but, of course, obstacles of all sorts present themselves in this quick moving and absorbing story of a man (Gauly) who is tormented by his inner conflicts and past history as a mercenary.
As the trio move across the world, there are many characters, situations, monsters, and "anomalies" ---- boss fights ---- that have to be dealt with along with a lot of exploration and things to discover that will keep you alert and interested in this nicely told story.
Character development gets high marks in this game ---- each of the main protagonists slowly reveal their true selves and their motivations as you get further into the tale. Gauly especially is believable and interesting.
High marks go to the music in the game, which sometimes adds to the suspenseful atmosphere, and sometimes offers relief in the form of light and catchy tunes ---- but is never overpowering.
Artwork is very good, particularly in the battle scenes. And the world itself is bright and colorful while caves, gloomy forests, etc. are presented in good detail.
The game offers a bit higher challenge in the beginning than most, but once you get the feel of how to battle and use magic the balance is just fine for moving along easily.
It's a classic 16-bit style rpg that is exciting and smoothly paced, and I'm glad it has arrived on Steam. I hope the sequel comes along soon.

So "Why am I recommending this game?" you ask?
I'm recommending it for the sake of the gameplay.
In a way this game reminds me of the original witcher game. That is because, like there, you deal with enemies posing real threat by preparing in advance. Each enemy has it's own quirks, strenghts, and weaknesses, and while they are not as tough as the videos make them look, they do pose enought threat to make you want to adapt to those strengths and weaknesses.
What makes the game hardly replayable is the fact that it's a lot more learning curve dependant than an average game. So for example, you'll get your fun from figureing out the way to get 5 enemies with one spike trap, but once you know how it's done there's nothing notably satisfying about that any more.
The story and visual style also remind me of the original witcher somewhat. That is because, like there, they are not "hollywoodish", which is a compliment in itself, if you ask me. Noting else good to say about them though - the game is visually poor and pale. And the story is bad in more ways than one... Rarely have I seen a story that's both religious enough to irritate atheists, occult/blasphemous enough to irritate monotheists, plain enough to bore the fans of the mystic themes, and bland enough not to impress a casual reader. I seriously can't imagine what they were thinking while making a game with that story...
That said, the games are meant to be played, not read or watched or heard (btw, the soundtrack here is great, if you ask me), and this game is worth playing.

This is gonna be more of a personal review than a general one. Let me start with saying that I had seen many many reviews about this game, a lot of them were negative some of them where OK but not reassuring. I'm a big fan of WWII shooters and despite the negative criticism towards Enemy Front, I wanted to give it a shot regardless. (You know sometimes we find some bad shooters and secretly enjoy them a little). Oh boy was I wrong on this one. So very wrong. I really wanted to enjoy Enemy Front, even if it was just a quick blast through the game and uninstall never to look back on, that would have been fine for me, considering I picked this game up during a sale for about 3$.
First impressions where not good. The game starts off with an incredibly boring and derivative setup. You're some kind of journalist-type who's in the midst of the world war, writing about the brave and strong people who fought and stood up to the Nazi oppression. I'll give it credit for being a little different and original, but the setup is easily forgettable moments after it's shown and isn't gripping enough to give a care in the world for.
The gameplay felt solid but clunky sometimes. I was given the opportunity very soon into the game to decide to take on an area with patrolling nazis either via stealth or by going loud and firing upon them. I decided to try the stealth approach. I was spotted magically around a corner of a wall, past a stack of crates, a bush and a doorway. Yup. The AI, to say the very least, is damn right dreadful. Stealth is not viable in Enemy Front and doesn't really work that well. Stealth takedowns are time consuming and quite frankly by the time you've hit your melee button you feel a sense of dread as you wait for a near 8 second long animation to play (doesn't sound like a lot but you sit there and count it and believe me you'll understand why it's annoying).
The gunplay is typically boring, each gun feels more or less the same, the only difference mainly being the fire-rate. The sound design is generic and poor quality. And the voice acting... my god, don't even get me started. Genuinely some of the worst voice acting I have ever experienced. (Resident Evil 1 and House of the Dead where memorable for having bad voice acting but this is just sad.)
I genuinely wanted to get some enjoyment out of this game, I really did. I wasn't expecting Enemy Front to be an amazing triple A product but I can honestly promise anyone interested - it is not worth the money and not even on sale. I picked Enemy Front up for 3$ and I've never requested a refund so quick in my life.
Enemy Front is a uninspiring, boring, dull, painstakinly abysmal shooter that offers nothing new or innovative. Play something better like the original Call of Duty games or Wolfenstein for a greater WWII game.

Most MMO's, your progress is determined by a 1 to 1 ratio of time to reward. The game controls this progression before hitting an "end game" of repeatable content.  Eve does not follow this model.  Instead your progress is controlled by your ability to excercise your own skills to build a niche for yourself inside of the community's social structure.  You decide your own goals, and even the smallest actions can influence the experience of hundreds if not thousands of players.  As one player you are often blind to these effects.
There are good and bad things about this model.  You start with nothing, and have to put in effort to get access to any of the tools that you feel you need.  The game does provide some pve content to grind towards these, but enterprising players will quickly realize that taking advantage of social relationships between players can accelerate them far faster than killing a bunch of computer controlled ships or mining a rock will. Making friends and building trust that will help supply ships, isk, or modules will help, but there's always the option of cashing in on that trust, and scamming people out of everything they own.  The best players will carve out unique niches for themselves, setting up businesses and fulfilling needs of the player groups around them while raking a profit in return.  None of this is easy, but for players that stick with it, Eve can be one of the most rewarding experiences in gaming.
In short, Eve is not for everyone.  It is slow, boring on the surface, but this rabbit hole of a game goes to the other end of the universe.  Give it a try.

Hello there good friend!
Say, do you like surviving against all odds? Do you like a city builder? Do you like RTS games? Have you ever played Prison Architect?
Well, if you do, take a blender, drop all of the above into it, with a cherry on top, and the result is: Rimworld!
Not to mention the number of mods and possible stories you can make out from it, and the game is a BETA, and it only became a beta about a week/two ago, but this is Beta done right, they might as well take the "Beta" away and say: "This is the game, everybody! Enjoy!"
Aside from this game being awesome, it also has Steam Workshop support, and a forum where you can download all sorts of mods, which, is kinda prone to pirates using it as a way to bypass Steam Workshop, but I do suggest looking at it from time to time, not all mods are uploaded to the workshop for some reason...
And now, to continue the tradition, let me tell you a story, at this point I won't say anything about the game, just something I came up with when playing around with the dev mode.
There was once a colony I built, dug into the mountain, it was a "Ferian" colony, essentially a utopia, well, except for one group.
The Colony was scientific, to the point where all the experiments were conducted on prisoners, who had decent personal cells, which, from raiding other colonies, one would consider a luxury! But, the ending of the game is where you build a spaceship.
I wanted to try it out for fun, and so, the Ferians(That I remodeled and remade to make them "Arctic") turned to the stars, to plant the banners of their faction on an unoccupied planet, and hopefully create a Glitterworld!
The colonists packed their stuff, and stepped into the cryosleep caskets, the ship took off and went into the night.
But, remember the prisoners? Well, starving, they finally, had a chance, to leave.
The colony's power shut down, it already being on emergency mode, the doors of the cells opened, the turrets were inactive, all that was left, was to step out, and... Leave.
But, you are weary, you already tried to, it ended badly, as shown by the still present gunshots wound that are yet to heal, so you wait until the rest leave, and you wait, and wait... You have no idea how long have you been waiting for, so far, no gunshots, you don't even hear footsteps, you step out at last, the sight of the turrets scares you, warily, you look over the corner... The turret doesn't react, it doesn't even move, scanning the area around it.
You step out, moving down the corridor...
It finally sinks in, the sheer size of the thing, holy bells! How are you going to get out of here?
You continue going down the corridor, and you can barely make out a sign that says "RIOT CONTROL - ARMORY", well well winner winner chicken dinner, you step inside, I take my words back, you loser, you are too late, the guns are taken, only the pain-sticks are left, well, at least something.
As you expect, a few dead bodies of a Na'hils, those are genocidal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, no wonder the three are lying dead, one of them was modified, that disturbs you, because seeing a thrumbo horn on a humanoid is a creepy sight and thought...
You take as much stuff as possible, going down the dark corridors, thankfully, with a flashlight!
You continue walking, as you see a sign saying "INDUSTRIAL/RESEARCH LEVEL", huh, those Ferians really like getting to the point, you would investigate it... But there is a door to your right, and it seems mighty interesting, well, because it's open, and the room inside is MASSIVE, you step in...
You wish you ignored it, aside from it being REALLY cold inside, you see... Dead bodies everywhere, and those aren't recent! Those are placed side by side, no blood, no clothes, NOTHING!
You see that one gal who was rumored to be given an Ovipositor... And it says on her dead body, that she died when trying to escape, from fatal damage to an ovipositor which lead to internal bleedings that weren't treated in time...
You stand there, thinking about what is this room even about, all you see is dead bodies and garbage, who would want to keep dead people in their base?!
You leave it, you remember the Research section, being a smart cookie in your colony, you realize what the bodies could be used for, you don't want to entertain that thought much, though...
You continue walking, as you finally reach the door, it feels like you are walking through a city, the place is just that massive... You open it, well, nothing creepy, the only thing is the extraordinary amount of machinery inside, things you NEVER SAW in your life, and this is probably the last time you will see it.
You notice, though, the door to the research sector, and as curious as a fox, you enter... Only to find even more machines you have NO IDEA about what they do.
Well, two doors... The Incubator, and storage.
You enter the former, it's closer, so it only makes sense, it's quite hot inside, the auto door(Which you now open manually) kept most of the heat inside, nothing inside of here, so, you leave.
Inside the latter, horror awaits...
"HUMANOID GENETIC MATERIAL", "RODENT GENETIC MATERIAL", "MUFFALO GENETIC MATERIAL", "AVIAN GENETIC MATERIAL", what does all of this mean? God, you see a box... "Human Ovipositor", you are once again, disturbed, you don't want to open, your curiosity backs off, as do you...
You leave the room disgusted, creeped out, you just want to LEAVE, you give out a sigh, you have to explore this facility fully, next time, you send a group to salvage this place, because you know you will never be able to get it operational.
You walk back, to see "Cafeteria", huh, not all words are bold and upper-case, it's obvious what's inside, but how does it look like?
You enter, and even under the light of a flashlight, it looks first, ENORMOUS, second, down-right beautiful, everything as clean as it gets, there is even food on the table with some Soda, praise the gods! You can finally eat something decent! And so you did, you have never in your life ate a meal like that, absolutely delicious, and with some Soda alongside it? What kind of place is this? You'd never be able to even get your hands on one of the Sodas, let alone drink it!
You continue and leave the cafeteria, going down the corridor that says "Living quarters", if they have such a cafeteria, what would the living quarters look like? Well, you found out, a sight you will truly never forget.
Inside of it, there were a few lamps powered by batteries, and the room, even light up, is something, you never wanted to leave.
Even the sight of a personal bathroom got you by surprise, you could never even THINK of something like that in your own colony, and the bed, decorated with gold and jade... So soft to lie on... And so you did, for a bit, you never wanted to stand up, but, with the conditions inside, you knew that, very soon, this place is subject for another raid, they happen all the time, this is the unbeatable jewel, someone wants to take the glory of raiding it, burning it to the floor, and taking everything inside.
You step out, depressed, you walk towards the exit...
You walk outside, the trees planet in a beautiful way, the flowers, you have no words to describe how it looks, and the lake decorated with statues, and bridges, you step on it, the sight is mesmerizing, but you HAVE to go now.
So, you step towards the area, you fear most, the defenses.
huh, you feared a reason, even turned off, this has the potential to scare off even the bravest of your colony, you look at it, all the turrets, guns down, no light, no sound, nothing, as quiet as it gets...
You continue walking forward, you... See many bodies, they seem to lack most of their body, as if it was ripped away... Disgusting, creepy, but, hopefully, they took most of it? Right, right?!
You continue, walking to the exit, at last! Fresh air, as cold as it is, the snow calms you down... What is that cli--- BOOM, you are thrown to the wall, breaking your spine, never to tell the tale.

UnReal World, AKA
, is the best survival roguelike game ever.  The game focuses on realism, and even simple choices you make early on have real and oftentimes deadly consequences.  Starving, freezing, drowning, illness, and bear attack are some of the ways you'll die.  And make no mistake about it, you'll die often.
With 20+ years of development history, its been improved and updated countless times to bring new features and enhance gameplay.  The random world generation and starting scenarios provide the only means of selecting difficulty.  Start the game hurt, in the middle of nowhere, in the dead of winter for a challenge, or start in a fully supplied friendly village for an easier time.
Build a homestead in the wilderness with all the amenities you need, or travel lightly and explore the random terrain.  Fishing, farming, trapping, and animal husbandry are some of the ways to sustain your existence.  Trade your goods with villagers and roaming travelers to obtain valuable items and tools you can't create yourself.  Hire companions to help you with your journey, or marry a villager and have her help make your life easier.
There's countless options on how to play and many choices to be made.  There's no right or wrong way, and no winning condition.  The only goal is to survive, and that is solely up to you.

If you are looking for a horror game that doesn't always use the typical methods, (predictable jump scares, loud music, hordes of creatures) is a decnt length for an episodic game, has a very interesting and enthralling story and has made great use of the tools it was given in the Half Life 2 engine then Estranged Act I is something you should definately try out. As a free to play, you have nothing to lose.
GAMEPLAY
As I said the game uses the Half Life 2 engine so nothing has really changed from movement, interaction or combat. There are a couple nice additions though such as interactable computers and the fact you are only allowed to carry one weapon at a time which gives it a nice realistic and survivalist feel. While not having a lot of combat, the horror is mostly made up of what you expect to happen but doesn't. I was yellnig at the game in my mind, "God damnit, just do what you're gonna do and get it over with already!" It's a very effective way to enduce fear as I found myself searching round corners a lot more than I usually would, your torch runs on dying batteries so I only used it for a couple seconds if I had to and I was reluctant to go into dark area's without preparing myself first. (I resisted the urge to turn on my television for noise in the background while I played. :) )
SOUND
A completely original soundtrack was used on this game and it stands out as a very eerie and unsettling score to represent how the character is feeling. There isn't really an ongoing ambient track and specific music only plays at certain parts.
But when the music isn't playing youre usually in silence which is extremely daunting as every noise can set you off. With only the gentle breeze passing by me and the chirping of the early morning birds, I found myself jumping everytime I accidentaly knocked over something on more than one occasion. Either just because it was loud enough to make me jump or I was worried that it would attract the "Yellow eyes." The team behind it has also employed their own voice actors to add a lot of original dialogue to the game to make it feel like a true standalone game. There are no re-used material of any of the Half Life or Source games, it's all them and they do an amazing job of it.
LOOK
Stunning graphics on an aging engine, they have made the game look miles better with their take on lighting. It's hard to explain exactly but the lighting makes the game feel so realistic. You walk under a streetlight and its bright all around you, but when you walk away it isn't just sudden;y darker, it gets darker gradually. That is the same with entering and exiting buildings, turning on lights or lights from computers and lamps etc.
STORY (MINOR SPOLIERS!)
The story is a very interesting one. You are a lone fisherman who's boat has just crashed onto a mysterious island which seems deserted... at first. Upon meeting a guy who lost his wife and daughter somewhere three months ago, you see him shoot a yellow eyed man in cold blood. When you set off on your own to find a way to exit the island you come across more of these monsters, strange communication arrays and an equally mysterious company known as Arque.
(MINOR SPOILERS END)
This is definately a game you do not want to miss. Hopefully soon they will bring out an Estranged Act II as there are many questions I need answers to. :)

Having beat the entire game and being a fan of WW2 era shooters, I would say unless you can find this game on sale what it offers is quite average. I still enjoyed my time with it overall, but I think many people may be disappointed other than diehard fans of FPS or the WWII setting.  I went into the game with low expectations, and certain things are done really well, most notably some of the level design (the cliffside castle with farms inparticular)  as well as familiar tropes including hillside towns with mortars, a submarine base, etc... And the presence of some semblance of stealth at times during the gameplay (similar to the Crysis games w/ display of enemies on the UI/map and their levels of alert...) make the game unique compared to other WW2 shooters.
The setting of Warsaw during the resistance uprising is a cool departure from the usually tread France, Germany, or Italy settings of other WW2 games, however the overall delivery of the story and characters is pretty bland. When other series such as Medal of Honor, COD, Sniper Elite, etc were around near when this game released make this game look like the underwhelming of most all of them by comparison.
The gameplay itself isn't bad, but my main complaint is that all of the weapons in a military / shooter game lack any real bass or punch to them. The familiar guns of the time all sound woefully bland and even the sniper rifle, grenades, or set explosives lack any real gusto to them. The effects are bland from their firing to the pitiful sound effects they each emit. In short, the combat (which there is plenty of) can be a bit boring/tame.
If you're REALLY itching for a WW2 shooter and don't mind some rough edges then it's not bad.

I admit, the game looks a little rough around the edges, but it's a phenomenal take on tower defense games .The cutscenes are a little cheesy, the graphics aren't all that great, but the gameplay is unparalleled. Each 'mission' you have a set amount of money to spend on traps... the more efficient you are at not wasting money, the more money you can spend on better gear/upgrades/etc. This creates a sort of minimalist approach.. you're constantly trying to place as little traps as possible, and setting up a perfect wave by wave traps and backup plans that you can fall back on if something doesn't hit. The feeling of satisfaction you get when you pull of a perfectly planned 5+ wave defense is like nothing I've felt before in a game. Even when something goes amiss and you manage to pull through by the skin of your teeth.. it's great. There's enough RPG skill tree mechanics and 3rd person fighting skill to make it a lot more 'alive' then your normal TD game, too. Buy it! You won't regret it.

Most MMO's, your progress is determined by a 1 to 1 ratio of time to reward. The game controls this progression before hitting an "end game" of repeatable content.  Eve does not follow this model.  Instead your progress is controlled by your ability to excercise your own skills to build a niche for yourself inside of the community's social structure.  You decide your own goals, and even the smallest actions can influence the experience of hundreds if not thousands of players.  As one player you are often blind to these effects.
There are good and bad things about this model.  You start with nothing, and have to put in effort to get access to any of the tools that you feel you need.  The game does provide some pve content to grind towards these, but enterprising players will quickly realize that taking advantage of social relationships between players can accelerate them far faster than killing a bunch of computer controlled ships or mining a rock will. Making friends and building trust that will help supply ships, isk, or modules will help, but there's always the option of cashing in on that trust, and scamming people out of everything they own.  The best players will carve out unique niches for themselves, setting up businesses and fulfilling needs of the player groups around them while raking a profit in return.  None of this is easy, but for players that stick with it, Eve can be one of the most rewarding experiences in gaming.

Writing a good film noir story is a lot trickier than it seems. A writer has to put together a fresh and kicking story line in spite of the mess of tropes that anyone attempting the genre has to follow (all broads are packin' heat, all cops are vultures, all private eyes drink heavily and have overactive internal monologue-glands, and 95% of everybody is lying to your face), and must do so in the most circuitous way possible, leaving a fine blend of clues, red herrings, and unintentional whatsits all over in order to keep the reader happy, confused, and eager to read on. At best, a failed attempt at film noir turns into a goofy comedy. At worst, you wind up with a pretentious pile that drags badly and signals whodunnit long before our antihero gets his teeth loosened at the tail end of a bad lead for the first time. Gunpoint actually manages to pull off a solid (if somewhat minimalist) film noir in the very unorthodox medium of 2D platform puzzler, and I couldn't be happier.
Set in a near- (if somewhat implausible) future, you play the poor sap who lives across the street from a major player in the small arms industry of America. Following recent legislation, firearms possession has become almost entirely illegal outside of police hands, but that doesn't stop you from getting embroiled in a trail of murder, betrayal, and espionage. Although initially motivated only by an urge to clear your name of a murder you had no part in, you quickly wind up playing for all parties involved, purchasing new gizmos and gadgets to aid you in breaking and entering along the way. While stealth gameplay is certainly a factor, more often than not you wind up making the building you're breaking into do all the hard work for you, "hacking" the electronics systems to work as you see fit. Make light switches open locked doors, power outlets taze guards, and motion detectors ignore you entirely, and you'll be able to acquire everything you need without winding up on the wrong end of a gun even once. Usually. Sometimes there's little choice besides punching someone's lights out, but more often than not you'll find that fights are best avoided.
The artwork's simple pixelwork, but it's charming all the same. The mechanics are fun and expand with each level, avoiding any chance of the gameplay going flat halfway through. Death is penalized only with a quick reload from your choice of the three most recent autosaves, and these are created every time you do anything of note. My only real gripes would be that the game's a little short and that the UI could've been a few notches crisper, but by and large I am very happy with this end product. A better way to burn through a gray September afternoon than a headful of bad memories and a rapidly-emptying bottle of forgetfulness.

My dad and his dad fought in WWII and as time passes and we get further away from these events and the immediacy of their impact I urge younger gamers to continue to acknowledge what happened by reading and viewing documentaries of WWII.   And of course even some games such as this can help stir your imagination.
This production shows a lot of effort in bringing to life an earlier era, in part by capturing the visual style of architecture, locations, uniforms, gear, vehicles and so on.  It is fair to say that the Polish developers took some pride in the visual recreation of images of the Warsaw uprising.
Picking this up for a bargain, there's no reason to bash this game because it shows a bit of age, or because "multiplayer is dead", but I do recommend that for whatever war games you choose to play, augment your experience by a bit of reading and reflection on the history of true events.

The core idea and story are great, especially for someone like me, a fan of horror films like Carpenter's The Thing, and someone who's always liked the idea of playing the monster in a game (whether misunderstood or just plain monstrous).
They've continued the interesting atmospheric world from the first game, where the military is brutal and uncaring as a whole, the corporations are greedy and amoral, but both contain sympathetic and helpful individuals.
And the gameplay is fairly simple, but somewhat challenging (at least on hard difficulty), and very good at making you feel like you're the evolved, shapeshifting, deadly soldier James Heller.
Note that my longer list of CONS below just indicates that I saw lots of room for improvement... but I still enjoyed the game.
PROS:
- Great story.
- A rare offering in a genre without many contenders.
- Some beautiful, visceral attack effects.
- Fun if simple gameplay.
CONS:
- The end battle really undoes the playstyle you develop through the rest of the game, sort of making you learn a new game.
- Littered with sexism and anti-intellectualism... and not all of it can be chalked up to "But that's just how this character thinks." Some of it is fundamental to the game's overall outlook.
- Some of the textures and modelling from the main game are too low-res for the in-game cutscenes. In those cases, they look awful.
- Not as sandbox-y as the first game.
- Character skills/customization is fairly broad and doesn't really let you specialize too much. So by late game, your character will play pretty much the same as any other playthrough.
- As a result of the above two points: not much replayability.
Rating: 8/10

Well, this came as a surprise, i mostly found out about it when i saw it on the steam homepage. I don't much care about remasters, but i DID get a nifty rebate due to owning the original version, and i could always do a third playthrough, so i went with it.
The game, in and of itself is the same. I mean, it is EXACTLY the same. So, if you liked or disliked something about the original, well..odds are you'll do so about this one too. However, that's not to say there's no value to this remaster. First of all, they fixed a few bugs that were rather annoying in the original (mostly, the inventory glitched and fired, making you waste ammo when selecting guns, or automatically switched to alcohol if you picked up a bottle), so that's a plus. Second, and most important, the game got a MAJOR visual overhaul, and i do mean MAJOR! Textures, effects, lighting, everything looks INCREDIBLE and, considering it is only a remaster of older graphics/models (Arkham Knight it won't be), it really does look, at worst, like a decent modern game, and, at best, like a beautiful work of art. (Exteriors, such as the beach, are a sight to behold).
So, is it worth it if you already have the original? At full price, maybe not, because the game IS exactly the same, but if you get a discount, then absolutely go for it. If nothing else, you'll love the GREATLY enhanced visuals, and the game will definitely feel fresh.
Now, if you never played Dead Island before, then definitely get this! It is without a doubt a TERRIFIC zombie game, looking better than ever, and playing even better!

As the Vault Hunters, you (and your friends) are looking for The Vault, a place that opens every 200 years, which, according to rumours, houses treasures not of this world. While it is a Pandoran legend, that's not going to stop you.
Borderlands is an open-world looter shooter with RPG elements. The enemies are usually bullet sponges, and while I'm of the philosophy that bullets shouldn't respect how far in the game you are, it's unavoidable. Weapons and other items are color-coded by rarity, and generally, by their overall quality. It goes as follows: White >> Green >> Blue >> Purple >> Orange, white being the most common, orange being the rarest. On another note entirely, vehicles drive like total♥♥♥♥♥ Fin.
You can choose one of four characters, each boasting a unique set of skills and a specific role in a well-balanced team.
Roland - the Soldier has a sentry turret which he can deploy, which, with some upgrades allows it to heal and replenish ammunition of teammates, filling a defensive and supportive role. The character is suited to shotguns and combat rifles.
Lilith - the Siren can phase out of reality as we perceive it, turning invisible to enemies and moving far faster than normal. With this, Lilith's elemental proficiency and her damage and crit skills in mind, the class is well-suited for a hit and run DPS role. The character is suited to SMGs and repeater pistols, preferably with the capability for elemental damage.
Mordecai - the Hunter can use his pet, Bloodwing to swoop in and attack enemies, dealing massive damage and negating cover. With his skills geared towards sniping and long-range combat, he fills in the much needed long-range role. The character is suited to revolvers and sniper rifles.
Brick - the Beserker can do just that, berserk his enemies, beating them into piles of bloody goop with his fists. His skills are geared towards tanking damage, kicking♥♥♥♥♥and taking names. The character is suited to explosives and melee combat.
The music is there, however, it's woefully average. There are a handful of memorable pieces, but it's mostly ambience and generic combat music.
This is a new addition to my typical reviews, but I've ought to mention this, the game is locked at a 55 degree field of view, which can understandably be troublesome for a lot of players. However, the performance is solid, which is a given since the game is approaching eight years of age.
If you enjoy RPGs, open worlds, shooting or looting, then this game is for you. While its sequel, Borderlands 2, overshadows it in every regard, I can't help but carry a certain degree of nostalgia towards the original. I have to say, that in my opinion, this is one of the finest looter shooters around, which isn't surprising when you consider that the market isn't crowded.

I'll start with pros and cons. Should work, everyone probably knows what that game is about.
Pros:
- Adds new effects and shaders to the original engine.
- Better textures and models.
- Fixed most of  the cutscene-related glitches. So most of the lipsync now works, and that scene when you get out of the supermarket now renders correctly.
- It's Dead Island, and I loved Dead Island.
Cons:
- While most of the graphical bugs and general glitches were fixed in the beginning of the game, as you progress through the story, you start seeing more and more of the old glitches found in the original. I think the prison level is just as bugged as it was in the original game, with a fair share of missing textures, missing geometry, empty rooms... The lab's (and some of the jungle's) containers are still mostly empty.
- The "gps" dotted path in your minimap only works for some objectives, lots of times, you get no path at all and have to rely on the map-screen or your personnal sense of direction.
- 'New Game Plus' is still completely asinine, xp-wise: you should be lvl 30+, the missions still give you the same ammount of xp as they did in your first playthrough, making zombie massacre the only viable way of levelling up.
